definition_zh: 果汁；汁液；精髓
definition_en: the liquid squeezed from fruit, vegetables, or meat, or the essential energy of something
core_image: 一只手把橙子对半切开，用力一挤，汁顺着指缝流下来
scene: 夏天的厨房里，桌上摊着果皮和切板，杯子里是刚榨出来的橙红色。A glass of fresh juice is all she wants at breakfast.
sceneCN: 这里 juice 是「果汁」（第 1 个义项：从果实压出的液体），句意为早餐她只想要一杯鲜果汁。画面里的物件：橙子、切板、玻璃杯。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -y 构成，义为「多汁的；有看头的」
由本词加 -er 构成，义为「榨汁机」
由本词加 -less 构成，义为「无汁的」

senses.title: Liquid from fruit
senses.definition: the liquid pressed or squeezed out of fruit or vegetables
senses.definitionCN: 从果实或蔬菜中压出的液体
senses.example: She drinks a glass of carrot juice every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天早上喝一杯胡萝卜汁。
senses.why: The fruit sense is the one English uses every day.
senses.whyCN: 果实的义项是英语每天在用的那一个。

senses.title: Liquid from meat
senses.definition: the natural liquid released from cooked meat
senses.definitionCN: 熟肉里自然渗出的液体
senses.example: Let the chicken rest so the juices stay in.
senses.exampleCN: 让鸡肉静置一会儿，肉汁才不会流失。
senses.why: Meat keeps the older, kitchen sense of the Latin word.
senses.whyCN: 肉汁保留了拉丁词更古老的厨房义。

senses.title: Energy or essence
senses.definition: the power that runs something, or the most essential part of it
senses.definitionCN: 让某物运转的动力，或某物最精华的部分
senses.example: The old radio needs new batteries; it has run out of juice.
senses.exampleCN: 这台老收音机要换电池，它没电了。
senses.why: Modern speech borrowed the liquid image for electric power, then for any energy.
senses.whyCN: 现代口语借「汁」的意象指电力，再扩展到任何能量。

intro.en: Juice came through Old French from Latin jus, which meant broth or juice.
intro.cn: juice 经古法语来自拉丁语 jus，意为肉汤或汁液。

items.en: jus meant "broth, juice, sauce".
items.cn: jus 意为「肉汤、汁、调味汁」。

items.en: French took it as jus, still used for gravy and law.
items.cn: 法语作 jus，既指肉汁也指法。

items.en: The form jus was borrowed into English as juice.
items.cn: jus 这一形式被英语借作 juice。

items.en: English used juice for the liquid of plants and fruit.
items.cn: 英语用 juice 指植物与果实的汁液。

items.en: Electricity gave the word a modern second life.
items.cn: 电力让这个词获得了现代的第二生命。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the jui- opening; the near-meaning group holds words for liquid and its essence.
note.cn: 形近组共用 jui- 开头；近义组收表示液体及其精华的词。

entries.definition: Full of juice, or full of interest.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「多汁的；有看头的」，同族词。

entries.definition: A machine for pressing fruit.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「榨汁机」，同族词。

entries.definition: Very large of its kind.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「特大号的」，拼写开头相同。

entries.definition: The liquid that carries food through a plant.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「树液」，植物生理用词。

entries.definition: Anything that flows and takes the shape of its vessel.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「液体」，最泛。

entries.definition: The most important quality of something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「精华」，偏抽象。

normalIntro.en: These hooks jump from a squeezed orange to a dying battery.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一个挤开的橙子跳到快没电的电池。

normal.en: jus in Latin was broth or juice.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 jus 是肉汤或汁。

normal.en: Squeeze an orange and the juice is what leaves.
normal.cn: 挤一个橙子，离开的就是汁。

normal.en: Add -y and the fruit becomes juicy.
normal.cn: 加 -y，果实就有了汁。

normal.en: A juicer is the machine that does the squeezing.
normal.cn: juicer 就是干这挤活的机器。

normal.en: A device without power has run out of juice too.
normal.cn: 没电的装置，也被说成「没汁了」。

abstract.en: Juice is the inside of a fruit made visible.
abstract.cn: 汁是果实内部露出来的样子。

abstract.en: What is squeezed out loses its shape but keeps its taste.
abstract.cn: 被挤出来的东西失了形状，却保住了味道。

abstract.en: Every engine lives on some kind of juice.
abstract.cn: 每台机器都靠某种「汁」活着。

examples.en: The children shared a carton of apple juice.
examples.cn: 孩子们分喝了一盒苹果汁。

examples.en: Lemon juice keeps sliced apples from browning.
examples.cn: 柠檬汁能让切开的苹果不变褐。

examples.en: The team has plenty of juice left for the last round.
examples.cn: 这支队伍还有足够的体力打最后一轮。

dict_mnemonic.text: juice 与 jus 同形：挤出来的东西

root: 拉丁语 jus「肉汤；汁」→ 古法语 jus → 中古英语 juice。同源有 justice（法）；派生有 juicy、juicer、juiceless。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: fruit liquid, meat juices, and the energy or essence that keeps something going.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：果实汁液、肉汁，以及维持某物的能量或精华。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an orange halved and pressed until liquid runs down the hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：橙子被挤开，汁顺着手指往下流。

branches.en: THE GLASS: fruit pressed into a drink.
branches.cn: 杯子这条线：果实被压成饮料。

branches.en: THE PLATE: meat keeping its liquid on the board.
branches.cn: 盘子这条线：肉在案板上留住汁水。

branches.en: THE BATTERY: the power that makes a thing run.
branches.cn: 电池这条线：让东西运转的动力。

branches.en: THE SQUEEZE: both senses are liquid taken from something.
branches.cn: 挤压这条线：两个义项都是从某物里取出的液体。

branches.en: THE CORE: what is inside is also what is essential.
branches.cn: 内核这条线：里面的东西也就是精华。

intro.en: Juice is a whole Latin stem borrowed through French, with a silent-e ending in English.
intro.cn: juice 是经法语借来的完整拉丁词干，英语里带一个不发音的 -e。

latinIntro.en: Latin jus stands behind juice; justice comes from the same Latin stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 jus 是 juice 的前身，justice 也出自同一词干。

items.example: It marks the long vowel in juice.
items.exampleCN: 它标出 juice 的长元音。

items.example: French kept both senses of the Latin.
items.exampleCN: 法语保留了拉丁语的两个义项。

items.example: A distant relative that kept the law sense.
The same ending extends the metaphor.
items.exampleCN: 同一词尾把比喻延伸出去。

definition_zh: 跳；跳跃；猛涨；跳过
definition_en: to push yourself off a surface into the air, or to rise or increase suddenly
core_image: 两脚同时离开地面，身体在半空中停住一瞬
scene: 跑道尽头，一个孩子数着数，腿一弯就蹬了出去。He jumped the fence and ran across the field.
sceneCN: 这里 jump 是「跳」（第 1 个义项：双脚蹬离地面），句意为他翻过栅栏穿过田野跑开。画面里的物件：跑道、栅栏、草地。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -er 构成，义为「跳跃者；毛衣（英式）」
由本词加 -y 构成，义为「紧张不安的」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「跳跃运动」

senses.title: Pushing off the ground
senses.definition: to leave the ground by bending the legs and pushing hard
senses.definitionCN: 屈腿用力蹬地离开地面
senses.example: The dog jumped into the water without hesitating.
senses.exampleCN: 那条狗毫不犹豫地跳进水里。
senses.why: The physical sense is the core, and every other use borrows its upward push.
senses.whyCN: 身体动作是核心，其他用法都借了那股向上的蹬力。

senses.title: Rising suddenly
senses.definition: to increase or rise quickly and by a large amount
senses.definitionCN: 迅速大幅度上升
senses.example: Prices jumped by a third in one month.
senses.exampleCN: 价格一个月里猛涨了三分之一。
senses.why: Numbers that rise suddenly behave like something springing up.
senses.whyCN: 突然上升的数字，像有东西弹了起来。

senses.title: Skipping over something
senses.definition: to cross over a fence or gap in one movement
senses.definitionCN: 一个动作跨过栅栏或空隙
senses.example: She jumped the low wall and was gone.
senses.exampleCN: 她跳过矮墙就不见了。
senses.why: The jump also covers the object jumped over.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也涵盖被跳过去的那个东西。

senses.title: Moving on too fast
senses.definition: to pass to a later point without the proper steps
senses.definitionCN: 跳过应有的步骤直接进入后面
senses.example: Do not jump to conclusions before the test results.
senses.exampleCN: 检查结果出来之前别急着下结论。
senses.why: Thinking can leap too, and skipping steps is the risky version.
senses.whyCN: 思维也会跳，跳过步骤就是有风险的那种。

intro.en: Jump is probably imitative, an English word of uncertain origin that simply sounds like a spring.
intro.cn: jump 很可能是拟声词，来源不确定，读音本身就带着一弹。

items.en: The word appears in English in the sixteenth century with no Latin ancestor.
items.cn: 这个词十六世纪出现在英语中，没有拉丁语祖先。

items.en: It was used of leaping animals and people alike.
items.cn: 它同时用于跳跃的动物和人。

items.en: The sense of a sudden rise in price came early.
items.cn: 价格猛涨的义项很早就出现了。

items.en: Sport fixed compounds such as long jump and high jump.
items.cn: 体育固定了 long jump、high jump 这样的复合词。

items.en: Idioms like jump at a chance keep the suddenness.
items.cn: jump at a chance 一类成语保留着那种突然。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the j- and -ump shape; the near-meaning group holds words for leaving the ground.
note.cn: 形近组共用 j- 与 -ump 的外形；近义组收表示离开地面的词。

entries.definition: One who jumps, or a knitted top.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「跳跃者；毛衣」，同族词。

entries.definition: Easily startled.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「容易受惊的」，同族词。

entries.definition: To knock against something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「碰撞」，只差一个字母。

entries.definition: To spring a long way through the air.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「跃」，距离更远。

entries.definition: To move on one leg or in small jumps.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「单脚跳」，幅度小。

entries.definition: To move suddenly upward.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「弹起」，强调弹力。

normalIntro.en: These hooks stay with the short, springy sound of the word.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子跟着这个词短促而有弹性的音。

normal.en: Say it fast and the mouth itself springs.
normal.cn: 快说一遍，嘴巴自己就弹了一下。

normal.en: No Latin behind it: the sound is the origin.
normal.cn: 背后没有拉丁语，声音就是来源。

normal.en: Prices jump like a startled animal.
normal.cn: 价格惊跳起来，像受惊的动物。

normal.en: Jump at a chance: the leap comes first, the thought later.
normal.cn: jump at a chance：先跳，后想。

normal.en: Add -y and you are jumpy, ready to startle.
normal.cn: 加 -y 就是 jumpy，随时会惊跳。

abstract.en: A jump is a small rebellion against gravity.
abstract.cn: 跳跃是对重力的一次小小反叛。

abstract.en: What goes up owes the ground a return.
abstract.cn: 跳起来的东西，都欠地面一次回程。

abstract.en: Most leaps are decided before the feet leave.
abstract.cn: 多数跃起，在脚离地之前就决定了。

examples.en: She jumped off the wall and landed badly.
examples.cn: 她从墙上跳下来，落地时扭到了。

examples.en: Sales jumped in the week before the holiday.
examples.cn: 假期前那一周销量猛增。

examples.en: Try not to jump from one idea to the next.
examples.cn: 尽量别从一个念头跳到下一个。

dict_mnemonic.text: jump 读音短促，本身就带一个弹起来的感觉

root: 来源不确定，可能为拟声词，十六世纪出现于英语。派生有 jumper、jumpy；无拉丁语同源。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: leaving the ground, rising fast, crossing in one move, and skipping ahead.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：蹬地跃起、迅速上升、一跨而过，以及跳过步骤。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: both feet leaving the ground and hanging for a moment.
core.cn: 核心意象：双脚离地，在半空停住一瞬。

branches.en: THE AIR: the body in flight.
branches.cn: 空中这条线：腾起的身体。

branches.en: THE CHART: a line that leaps upward.
branches.cn: 曲线这条线：一下窜上去的线。

branches.en: THE WALL: the fence taken in one move.
branches.cn: 矮墙这条线：一步跨过去的栅栏。

branches.en: THE GAP: steps left out on purpose or by haste.
branches.cn: 空缺这条线：有意或匆忙落下的步骤。

branches.en: THE SURPRISE: both senses break an expected line.
branches.cn: 意外这条线：两个义项都打断了预期。

intro.en: Jump has no prefix or suffix in its base form; it is a single Germanic-style root of uncertain origin.
intro.cn: jump 原形没有前后缀，是一个来源不明的单一词根。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source, so latinEntries stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 它没有拉丁语来源，所以 latinEntries 留空。

items.example: Sport builds compounds on the word.
items.exampleCN: 体育在它上面造复合词。

definition_zh: 年少的；初级的；资历较浅的；下级的；职位低的；较年轻者
definition_en: younger in age, or lower in rank or experience than someone else
core_image: 队列里排在后面、个子还矮一头的那个新人
scene: 办公室里最新的那个人坐在靠门的位置，桌上只摆着一台旧电脑。As a junior clerk, he handled the files nobody else wanted.
sceneCN: 这里 junior 是「初级的、资历浅的」（第 1 个义项：在职位或经验上低于他人），句意为作为初级职员，他处理没人愿意管的档案。画面里的物件：办公室、靠门的桌子、旧电脑。

pos.zh: 形容词：年少的；初级的；资历浅的；下级的
名词：较年轻者；下级；初级职员

derivatives.zh: 由 junior 加 -ity 构成，义为「资历较浅的状态」
由 junior 加 -ate 构成，指修会培养期或初级阶段

senses.title: Lower in rank or experience
senses.definition: having a lower position or less experience than others in the same organization
senses.definitionCN: 在同一机构中职位较低或经验较少
senses.example: She started as a junior designer in the studio.
senses.exampleCN: 她在工作室从初级设计师做起。
senses.why: Rank is the comparison that matters most in offices, staff against staff.
senses.whyCN: 在办公室里最重要的比较是职位，是员工与员工之间的比较。

senses.title: Younger in age
senses.definition: younger than another person, often used of a son named after his father
senses.definitionCN: 年龄小于他人，常用于父子同名的场合
senses.example: He is three years junior to his brother.
senses.exampleCN: 他比哥哥小三岁。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply younger, and it still keeps the Latin comparison.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的一层意思就是「更年轻」，它仍保留着拉丁语比较级的底子。

senses.title: Of the lower school level
senses.definition: relating to the earlier part of a school or a college year
senses.definitionCN: 指学校的低年级阶段或大学三年级
senses.example: She teaches at a junior school near the park.
senses.exampleCN: 她在公园附近的一所小学教书。
senses.why: Schools borrow the age comparison and turn it into a stage of study.
senses.whyCN: 学校借用了年龄比较，把它变成一个学段。

senses.title: A person of lower rank
senses.definition: a person who holds a lower position than someone else
senses.definitionCN: 职位低于他人的人
senses.example: The partners rarely listen to the juniors.
senses.exampleCN: 合伙人很少听下属的意见。
senses.why: The adjective turns into a person: the lower-ranked member of the team.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成一个人：团队中位次较低的那个成员。

senses.title: Smaller in a competition class
senses.definition: belonging to a younger age group in sport or contests
senses.definitionCN: 指体育或竞赛中属于较年轻年龄组
senses.example: He won the junior title at fifteen.
senses.exampleCN: 他十五岁就拿下了少年组冠军。
senses.why: Sport turns age into a class, with its own titles and records.
senses.whyCN: 体育把年龄变成一个组别，有自己的冠军和纪录。

senses.title: The third college year
senses.definition: in American usage, the third year of a four-year course
senses.definitionCN: 美式用法中指四年制课程的第三年
senses.example: She spent her junior year abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 她大三那年去了国外。
senses.why: In a four-year course the third year is junior to the last one.
senses.whyCN: 在四年制课程里，第三年比上年一级「低」，于是叫 junior year。

intro.en: Junior was borrowed from Latin junior, the comparative of juvenis, young; English uses it unchanged.
intro.cn: junior 直接借自拉丁语 junior，是 juvenis「年轻」的比较级；英语原样沿用。

items.en: juvenis meant young, and junior was its comparative form.
items.cn: juvenis 意为年轻的，junior 是它的比较级。

items.en: The -or ending marks the comparative, as in senior.
items.cn: -or 词尾标记比较级，senior 也是如此。

items.en: English borrowed junior in the sixteenth century as an adjective and noun.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 junior，兼作形容词和名词。

items.en: The rank sense spread through offices and armed forces.
items.cn: 「职位较低」这一义在机关和军队中扩散。

items.en: The school senses, junior school and junior year, settled in the modern period.
items.cn: 初级学校与大学三年级等教育义在近现代固定下来。

note.en: The look-alike group holds Latin comparatives that end in -or; the near-meaning group holds words for younger and lower rank.
note.cn: 形近组收以 -or 结尾的拉丁比较级；近义组收表示年幼与低级的词。

entries.definition: Older or higher in rank.
entries.definitionCN: junior 的反义对应词，义为「年长的；高级的」。

entries.definition: Young, or a young person.
entries.definitionCN: 同源于 juvenis，义为「少年的」。

entries.definition: The state of being junior.
entries.definitionCN: 派生名词，指资历较浅的状态。

entries.definition: Less old than another person.
entries.definitionCN: 最简单直白的「更年轻的」。

entries.definition: Lower in rank within a system.
entries.definitionCN: 较正式，指体制中下级。

entries.definition: Someone being trained for a job.
entries.definitionCN: 指正在受训的岗位新人。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from the Latin comparative ending to the desk by the door.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从拉丁语比较级词尾走到靠门的那张桌子。

normal.en: Junior is the comparative of juvenis, young.
normal.cn: junior 是 juvenis「年轻」的比较级。

normal.en: The pair junior and senior is fixed in offices and schools.
normal.cn: junior 与 senior 这一对在机关和学校都固定。

normal.en: Junior to someone uses to, not than.
normal.cn: junior to someone 用 to，不用 than。

normal.en: Junior high school covers the early teenage years.
normal.cn: junior high school 指初中阶段。

normal.en: In American colleges junior year is the third year.
normal.cn: 美国大学的 junior year 是第三年。

abstract.en: A junior is one row back in the same line.
abstract.cn: 初级者是在同一条队伍里后退一排的人。

abstract.en: The word is a comparison, so it always needs another person.
abstract.cn: 这个词是比较，因此总需要另一个人才成立。

abstract.en: Everyone is junior to someone, and senior to someone else.
abstract.cn: 每个人对某些人初级，对另一些人高级。

examples.en: Two junior staff members handled the whole report.
examples.cn: 两名初级员工完成了整份报告。

examples.en: My sister is junior to me by two years.
examples.cn: 我妹妹比我小两岁。

examples.en: He is looking for a junior position in design.
examples.cn: 他在找一个设计方面的初级职位。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「就是你儿」—— 家里年纪最小的那个，就是初级选手

root: 拉丁语 juvenis「年轻的」→ 比较级 junior → 英语 junior，原样借用；同族的反义比较级是 senior。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses: lower rank, younger age, lower school level, a lower-ranked person, a younger contest class, and the third college year.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项：职位较低、年纪较小、学校初段、下级人员、少年组，以及大学三年级。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one person standing a row behind and half a head lower.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在后退一排、矮半头的位置。

branches.en: THE OFFICE: a new desk and the files nobody wants.
branches.cn: 办公室这条线：新桌子与没人要的档案。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: the son who shares the father's name.
branches.cn: 家庭这条线：与父亲同名的儿子。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL: early years and the third college year.
branches.cn: 学校这条线：低年级与大学三年级。

branches.en: THE FIELD: the younger age bracket of a contest.
branches.cn: 赛场这条线：比赛的较年轻年龄组。

branches.en: THE LADDER: every rung is junior to the one above.
branches.cn: 梯子这条线：每一级都低于它上面那一级。

intro.en: Junior is a Latin comparative borrowed whole; English adds only a few endings.
intro.cn: junior 是整体借来的拉丁比较级，英语只添了少数词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin relatives all grow from juvenis, young.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词都从 juvenis「年轻」长出来。

items.exampleCN: 它构成 junior 与 senior。

items.example: More junior is the periphrastic form.
items.exampleCN: more junior 是分析式比较级。

definition_zh: 正好；仅仅；刚刚；只是；公正的；恰好的
definition_en: exactly at that point, only a moment ago, merely, or fair and right
core_image: 一根线刚好对齐刻度，不多一分也不少一分
scene: 两个人在门口互相看了一眼，谁都没说话。He was just leaving when the phone rang.
sceneCN: 这里 just 是「刚要」（第 1 个义项：正好处在某个时点上），句意为他正要出门时电话响了。画面里的物件：门口、外套、响起的电话。

pos.zh: 副词：正好；刚刚；仅仅；只是；简直
形容词：公正的；正当的；恰当的

derivatives.zh: 由 just 加 -ice 构成，义为「正义；司法」
由 just 加 -ly 构成，义为「公正地」
由 just 加 -ify 构成，义为「证明正当」
加前缀 un- 构成，义为「不公正的」

senses.title: Exactly at a point in time or space
senses.definition: exactly at a particular moment, or exactly at a place or amount
senses.definitionCN: 恰好在某一时刻，或恰好是某处、某个量
senses.example: The train arrived just as we reached the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 我们刚到闸口，火车就到了。
senses.why: The oldest core is exactness: neither earlier nor later, neither more nor less.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的核心是「恰好」：不早不晚，不多不少。

senses.title: A very short time ago
senses.definition: a very short time ago, in the immediate past
senses.definitionCN: 刚刚过去的一小段时间
senses.example: She has just called from the station.
senses.exampleCN: 她刚从车站打来电话。
senses.why: A point so close to now that it barely qualifies as past.
senses.whyCN: 一个离现在极近的时刻，勉强算作过去。

senses.title: Only or merely
senses.definition: no more than the stated amount or thing
senses.definitionCN: 不超过所说的数量或事物
senses.example: It was just a small mistake.
senses.exampleCN: 那只是个小错误。
senses.why: Exactness narrows to a single item, leaving everything else outside.
senses.whyCN: 「恰好」收窄到只有一个，其他都被排除在外。

senses.title: Fair according to what is right
senses.definition: acting or given in accordance with what is right and deserved
senses.definitionCN: 依照正当标准行事或给予的
senses.example: A just settlement was reached within a week.
senses.exampleCN: 一周内达成了公正的解决方案。
senses.why: The adjective sense moves from exact measure to fair measure: what is deserved to a hair.
senses.whyCN: 形容词义从精确的度量走到公平的度量：应得的一丝不差。

senses.title: Barely enough or almost not
senses.definition: only barely, so that the result is almost the opposite
senses.definitionCN: 指仅仅勉强达到，结果几乎相反
senses.example: We just made it before the gate closed.
senses.exampleCN: 我们刚好在关门前进去了。
senses.why: The exactness of just is stretched to its limit: one second more and it fails.
senses.whyCN: 「恰好」被拉到极限：再多一秒就不成了。

senses.title: Used to soften a request or statement
senses.definition: in a request, used to make the tone lighter or politer
senses.definitionCN: 请求中用来让语气更轻或更客气
senses.example: Could you just wait outside for a moment?
senses.exampleCN: 你能在外面稍等一会儿吗？
senses.why: Just here lowers the weight of a request, asking for the smallest possible amount.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 just 减轻了请求的分量，只要求最小的那一点。

intro.en: Just comes from Latin justus, "lawful, right", from jus, law; the same word therefore covers both exactness and fairness.
intro.cn: just 来自拉丁语 justus「合法的、正当的」，源词 jus「法」；因此它同时覆盖「恰好」与「公正」两面。

items.en: jus meant law or right, and justus meant conforming to it.
items.cn: jus 意为法或权利，justus 意为符合法的。

items.en: Old French juste kept the sense of right and exactly fitting.
items.cn: 古法语 juste 保留了「正当」与「恰好合适」两种意思。

items.en: English borrowed just as both adjective and adverb in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪把 just 兼作形容词和副词借入。

items.en: The exactness sense, just right or just now, grew from fitting perfectly.
items.cn: 「恰好」义从「完全契合」发展而来。

items.en: The merely sense developed from the idea of exactly this and no more.
items.cn: 「仅仅」义从「恰好只有这些，不多」发展而来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin jus root; the near-meaning group holds adverbs of time, degree, and fairness.
note.cn: 形近组共用拉丁 jus 词根；近义组收时间、程度与公平类副词。

entries.definition: Fairness, or the legal system.
entries.definitionCN: 同源名词，义为「正义；司法」。

entries.definition: In a fair way.
entries.definitionCN: 由 just 加 -ly 构成，义为「公正地」。

entries.definition: To show that something is right.
entries.definitionCN: 同源动词，义为「证明正当」。

entries.definition: No more than; merely.
entries.definitionCN: 副词义为「仅仅」，与第 3 个义项最近。

entries.definition: With no difference at all.
entries.definitionCN: 副词义为「恰好」，与第 1 个义项最近。

entries.definition: Treating people equally and rightly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「公平的」，与第 4 个义项最近。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from Latin law to the moment before the phone rings.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从拉丁语的「法」走到电话响前的那个瞬间。

normal.en: Latin jus, law, is the root of just, justice, and justify.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 jus「法」是 just、justice、justify 的共同词根。

normal.en: Just as means at the same instant that something else happens.
normal.cn: just as 表示另一件事正在发生的同一瞬间。

normal.en: Just now means a moment ago, not at this instant.
normal.cn: just now 指刚才，而不是此刻。

normal.en: Just a moment is the polite way to ask for a short wait.
normal.cn: just a moment 是请人稍等的客气说法。

normal.en: The adjective just is rare in speech but regular in law and argument.
normal.cn: 形容词 just 口语少用，但在法律和论证里很常见。

abstract.en: Just is a line laid exactly on a mark.
abstract.cn: just 就是把线正压在刻度上。

abstract.en: The same word measures time and measures fairness.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既量时间，也量公平。

abstract.en: Exactness and justice are both a matter of not tipping the scale.
abstract.cn: 精确与公正，都是不让秤歪。

examples.en: The phone rang just as I sat down.
examples.cn: 我刚坐下电话就响了。

examples.en: He has just finished the last page.
examples.cn: 他刚刚看完最后一页。

examples.en: It was just a joke, nothing more.
examples.cn: 那只是个玩笑，没别的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扎死特」—— 分寸掐得正正好，分毫不差

root: 拉丁语 jus「法、权利」→ justus「合法的、正当的」→ 古法语 juste → 英语 just；同族 justice、justify、justly。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses: exactness in time, the immediate past, mere amount, fairness, bare sufficiency, and a softening request.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项：时间或位置的恰好、刚刚过去、仅仅、公正、勉强够，以及缓和语气的「稍」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line set exactly on the mark, no slip either way.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根线正压在刻度上，两边都不偏。

branches.en: THE PLATFORM: the train meets the moment you arrive.
branches.cn: 站台这条线：火车正好在你到时进站。

branches.en: THE PHONE: a call from a minute ago.
branches.cn: 电话这条线：一分钟前打来的。

branches.en: THE SMALL WORD: merely, and a gentle please wait.
branches.cn: 小小的语气词：仅仅，以及客气地请人稍等。

branches.en: THE SCALES: what someone deserves, to a hair.
branches.cn: 天平这条线：一个人应得的分毫不差。

branches.en: THE CLOSING GATE: through by a centimetre.
branches.cn: 关门这条线：差一厘米就进不来。

intro.en: Just is the bare Latin adjective; its family takes Latin and English endings.
intro.cn: just 是裸露的拉丁形容词，它的词族要加拉丁或英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin relatives descend from jus, law, and justus, lawful.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词源自 jus「法」与 justus「合法的」。

definition_zh: 保持；保存；保留；继续；饲养；遵守；照料
definition_en: to continue to have or hold something, or to stay in a state without changing
core_image: 手里紧紧攥着一样东西，怎么也不松
scene: 搬家时他把一箱旧信留在角落，谁劝也不肯扔。He kept every letter she ever sent him.
sceneCN: 这里 keep 是「保存、保留」（第 2 个义项：留着不丢弃），句意为她寄来的每封信他都留着。画面里的物件：一箱旧信、搬家纸箱、角落。

pos.zh: 动词：保持；保留；保存；继续；饲养；遵守
名词：生计；饲养费用（keep of a horse）

derivatives.zh: 由 keep 加 -er 构成，义为「看守人；守门员」
由 keep 加 -ing 构成，义为「保管；一致」
由 up 加 keep 构成，义为「维护费用」
复合名词，义为「妥善保管」

senses.title: To stay in a state
senses.definition: to continue to be in a particular state or condition
senses.definitionCN: 继续处在某种状态
senses.example: Keep calm and read the question again.
senses.exampleCN: 保持冷静，把题目再读一遍。
senses.why: The core is continuation: the state does not change.
senses.whyCN: 核心是延续：状态不发生变化。

senses.title: To retain possession of
senses.definition: to continue to have something and not give it away or lose it
senses.definitionCN: 继续拥有某物，不送出也不丢失
senses.example: You can keep the book; I have another copy.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书你留着吧，我还有一本。
senses.why: Retaining is continuation applied to an object in the hand.
senses.whyCN: 保留就是把「延续」用在手里的一件东西上。

senses.title: To do something repeatedly
senses.definition: to continue doing something, often again and again
senses.definitionCN: 持续做某事，常指一再发生
senses.example: She kept looking at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 她一直朝门口看。
senses.why: Repeating an act is continuing it, so the same verb covers both.
senses.whyCN: 反复做同一个动作就是把它延续下去，同一个动词因此兼顾两者。

senses.title: To care for or raise animals
senses.definition: to own and look after animals such as bees or chickens
senses.definitionCN: 指拥有并照料蜜蜂、鸡等动物
senses.example: They keep bees behind the barn.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在谷仓后面养蜂。
senses.why: Looking after animals is holding them over time, at a steady cost.
senses.whyCN: 照料动物就是长期持有，并付出持续的开销。

senses.title: To observe or honour a rule
senses.definition: to act in accordance with a law, promise, or custom
senses.definitionCN: 依照法律、承诺或习俗去做
senses.example: Everyone kept the silence until the bell rang.
senses.exampleCN: 大家一直保持安静，直到铃响。
senses.why: Honouring a rule is keeping it in force, the same holding seen from the rule side.
senses.whyCN: 遵守规则就是让规则继续有效，是同一个「持有」从规则那边看。

senses.title: The cost of living or upkeep
senses.definition: the food and cost needed to maintain a person or animal
senses.definitionCN: 维持人或动物所需的食物与花费
senses.example: The keep of a horse is no small sum.
senses.exampleCN: 养一匹马的开销可不小。
senses.why: The noun names what must be handed over to keep something alive.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指为了把某物养活下去必须付出的东西。

intro.en: Keep comes from Old English cepan, to seize or take heed, and the sense shifted from grabbing to holding.
intro.cn: keep 来自古英语 cepan「抓住、留意」，词义从「抓取」滑向「持有」。

items.en: cepan meant to seize, to take heed, or to watch over.
items.cn: cepan 意为抓取、留意或看守。

items.en: The sense of watching gave keepers and keeping guard.
items.cn: 「看守」义后来生出 keeper 与 keep guard。

items.en: Middle English keep broadened to hold, retain, and continue.
items.cn: 中古英语 keep 扩展到持有、保留、持续。

items.en: Keep doing became the standard pattern for continuing an action.
items.cn: keep doing 成为表示「持续做」的标准结构。

items.en: The noun keep survives in the keep of an animal and in upkeep.
items.cn: 名词 keep 保留在动物饲养费与 upkeep 中。

note.en: The look-alike group holds short look-alikes of keep; the near-meaning group holds verbs of holding and continuing.
note.cn: 形近组收与 keep 相似的短词；近义组收表示持有与持续的词。

entries.definition: Eager or sharp.
entries.definitionCN: 拼写只差一个字母，义为「热切的；锋利的」。

entries.definition: The past form of keep.
entries.definitionCN: keep 的过去式和过去分词。

entries.definition: Someone who looks after something.
entries.definitionCN: 由 keep 加 -er 构成，指看守人或守门员。

entries.definition: To have something in the hands.
entries.definitionCN: 指手里拿着，最具体。

entries.definition: To keep something in good condition.
entries.definitionCN: 较正式，指维持良好状态。

entries.definition: To keep something rather than lose it.
entries.definitionCN: 较正式，强调不失去。

normalIntro.en: These hooks run from Old English cepan, to seize, to a box of letters in the corner.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从古英语 cepan「抓取」走到角落那箱旧信。

normal.en: Old English cepan meant to seize and also to watch over.
normal.cn: 古英语 cepan 既指抓取，也指看守。

normal.en: Keep doing means keep on doing, without a break.
normal.cn: keep doing 意为一再做，不间断。

normal.en: Kept is the only past form; there is no keeped.
normal.cn: 过去式只有 kept，没有 keeped。

normal.en: Keeper adds -er to make the person.
normal.cn: keeper 加 -er 变成人。

normal.en: Keep in touch fixes the retaining sense in daily use.
normal.cn: keep in touch 把「保持」义留在日常里。

abstract.en: To keep is to refuse to let the moment pass.
abstract.cn: 保留就是不让那一刻过去。

abstract.en: The same word holds an object, a habit, and a silence.
abstract.cn: 同一个词能留住东西、习惯和一份安静。

abstract.en: A keeper is one who holds a door open for others.
abstract.cn: keeper 是替别人扶住门的人。

examples.en: Please keep the door closed at night.
examples.cn: 夜里请把门关着。

examples.en: She kept the old ticket in her wallet.
examples.cn: 她一直把那张旧票留在钱包里。

examples.en: He kept asking the same question.
examples.cn: 他一直在问同一个问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「k皮」—— 把皮牢牢攥住，就是保留下来

root: 古英语 cepan「抓取；留意；看守」→ 中古英语 keep「持有；保留；继续」→ 现代英语 keep；过去式 kept。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses: staying in a state, retaining an object, doing something repeatedly, keeping animals, obeying a rule, and the cost of upkeep.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项：保持状态、保留物件、一再做某事、饲养动物、遵守规则，以及饲养费用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand closed tight around something, not letting go.
core.cn: 核心意象：手紧紧攥住一样东西，不放手。

branches.en: THE SHUT DOOR: a state left exactly as it was.
branches.cn: 关着的门这条线：状态原封不动。

branches.en: THE BOX OF LETTERS: things kept and never thrown out.
branches.cn: 信箱这条线：留着从不丢的东西。

branches.en: THE REPEATED QUESTION: an action that goes on.
branches.cn: 反复的提问这条线：持续不断的行为。

branches.en: THE HIVES: animals looked after, at a cost.
branches.cn: 蜂箱这条线：照料动物，也要花钱。

branches.en: THE PROMISE: a rule held to without exception.
branches.cn: 承诺这条线：不打折扣地遵守。

intro.en: Keep is a native verb; English endings build its family with no Latin stem.
intro.cn: keep 是本族动词，词族全靠英语词尾，没有拉丁词干。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root behind keep, so the list below stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: keep 背后没有拉丁词根，因此下面留空。

definition_zh: 钥匙；关键；答案；键；（音乐）调
definition_en: a shaped piece of metal that opens a lock, or the most important part of something
core_image: 一片齿形金属插进锁孔，转半圈，锁舌应声收回
scene: 房东把一串叮当响的东西交给他，说楼下信箱也要用同一片。He turned the key twice and the door opened.
sceneCN: 这里 key 是「钥匙」（第 1 个义项：开锁的金属片），句意为他拧了两下钥匙，门开了。画面里的物件：门锁、钥匙串、门口。

pos.zh: 名词：钥匙；关键；答案；键；调
动词：键入；使适应（key in / key to）

derivatives.zh: 复合词，指键盘
复合词，指锁孔
复合词，指关键词
加 -less 构成，义为「无钥匙的」
加 -ed 构成，义为「（情绪上）紧张的；已键入的」

senses.title: A shaped metal piece for a lock
senses.definition: a small metal object cut to fit a lock and work its bolt
senses.definitionCN: 按锁孔形状切制、用来开锁的小金属件
senses.example: She keeps a spare key under the mat.
senses.exampleCN: 她在门口的垫子下面留了一把备用钥匙。
senses.why: The core object is shaped to one lock and has no other use.
senses.whyCN: 核心物件只为一把锁成形，别无他用。

senses.title: The most important element
senses.definition: the thing that makes success possible or explains a problem
senses.definitionCN: 使成功成为可能或能解释问题的那个要素
senses.example: Patience is the key to learning a language.
senses.exampleCN: 耐心是学语言的关键。
senses.why: Access turns into explanation: the key opens a problem, not just a door.
senses.whyCN: 「开启」变成「解释」：钥匙打开的不只是门，还有问题。

senses.title: A set of answers or symbols
senses.definition: a list explaining the answers to exercises or the symbols on a map
senses.definitionCN: 解释习题答案或地图符号的说明表
senses.example: Check your answers against the key.
senses.exampleCN: 对照答案核对你的结果。
senses.why: The list that unlocks the exercises borrows the same image of opening.
senses.whyCN: 打开习题的那张表，借用了同一个「开启」的画面。

senses.title: A button pressed with a finger
senses.definition: one of the parts of a keyboard, piano, or similar instrument
senses.definitionCN: 键盘、钢琴等上面按下的部件
senses.example: The letter key is worn away.
senses.exampleCN: 那个字母键已经磨平了。
senses.why: A pressed button works like a small lock that opens a letter.
senses.whyCN: 按下的键就像一把打开字母的小锁。

senses.title: The tonal centre of a piece
senses.definition: the scale in which a piece of music is written
senses.definitionCN: 一首乐曲所依据的调式
senses.example: The song moves into a brighter key.
senses.exampleCN: 这首歌转进了一个明快的调。
senses.why: One note governs where the melody can go, as a key governs a door.
senses.whyCN: 一个音决定旋律能往哪走，正如钥匙决定门。

senses.title: To type in data
senses.definition: to enter information by pressing keys
senses.definitionCN: 通过按键录入信息
senses.example: Key in your name and press enter.
senses.exampleCN: 输入姓名后按回车。
senses.why: Typing is pressing keys in order, one opening after another.
senses.whyCN: 打字就是按顺序按键，一次次开启。

senses.title: Crucially important
senses.definition: most important for a result or explanation
senses.definitionCN: 对结果或解释最为重要
senses.example: Timing was a key factor in the win.
senses.exampleCN: 时机是这次获胜的关键因素。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the idea of the single decisive part.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留了「唯一决定性部分」这个想法。

intro.en: Key comes from Old English cǣg, a key, a native Germanic word with no known deeper origin.
intro.cn: key 来自古英语 cǣg「钥匙」，是本族日耳曼词，更早的源头已不可考。

items.en: cǣg meant a key for a lock and had no similar Latin source.
items.cn: cǣg 意为开锁的钥匙，并无对应的拉丁来源。

items.en: Middle English keye spread the sense to a means of explanation.
items.cn: 中古英语 keye 把词义扩展到「解释的途径」。

items.en: The musical key sense grew from the idea of a controlling scale.
items.cn: 音乐上的「调」义从「决定全曲的音阶」发展而来。

items.en: The keyboard gave the button sense in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 十九世纪的键盘带来了「键」这一义。

items.en: The adjective and verb key, as in key in, are modern extensions.
items.cn: 形容词 key 与动词 key in 都是近现代扩展。

note.en: The look-alike group holds short forms of the key family and its look-alikes; the near-meaning group holds words for importance.
note.cn: 形近组收 key 词族及其外形相近的词；近义组收表示重要性的词。

entries.definition: The panel of keys on a piano or computer.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词，指钢琴或电脑的键盘。

entries.definition: The opening for a key in a lock.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词，指锁孔。

entries.definition: A platform where ships load.
entries.definitionCN: 发音相同而拼写不同，指码头。

entries.definition: Decisive for an outcome.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「决定性的」。

entries.definition: Needed in order to exist or work.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「必不可少的」。

entries.definition: A piece of evidence that helps solve something.
entries.definitionCN: 指帮助解谜的线索，与「钥匙」比喻相近。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a cut piece of metal to a key on a keyboard.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一片切好的金属走到键盘上的一个键。

normal.en: The key to something uses to, not of.
normal.cn: key to something 用 to，不用 of。

normal.en: Under lock and key means safely shut away.
normal.cn: under lock and key 指锁得好好的。

normal.en: A key answers a puzzle, a lock, or an exam paper.
normal.cn: key 既能解谜、开锁，也能对答案。

normal.en: Key in is the verb for typing numbers.
normal.cn: key in 是键入数字的动词用法。

normal.en: Music keys and keyboard keys both come from the same controlling idea.
normal.cn: 音乐上的调与键盘上的键都来自「决定、支配」这一想法。

abstract.en: A key is a small piece of metal shaped to one lock only.
abstract.cn: 钥匙是只为一把锁塑形的一小片金属。

abstract.en: The same word can be an object, a place, and a reason.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既可以是物件、是位置，也可以是理由。

abstract.en: Every problem has a lock somewhere, and often a key too.
abstract.cn: 每个问题都有一把锁，通常也有一把钥匙。

examples.en: I left my keys inside the car.
examples.cn: 我把钥匙落在车里了。

examples.en: Communication is the key to good teamwork.
examples.cn: 沟通是好团队合作的关键。

examples.en: Key in the code and the door opens.
examples.cn: 输入密码，门就开了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ki 钥匙」—— 一插进去，锁就开了

root: 古英语 cǣg「钥匙」，本族日耳曼词，更深来源不明；后引申出「关键、调、键」等义。

sensesIntro.en: Seven senses: the metal key, the crucial element, an answer list, a button, a musical key, typing data, and the adjective for importance.
sensesIntro.cn: 七个义项：金属钥匙、关键、答案表、键、乐调、输入数据，以及表示重要的形容词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cut piece of metal shaped to fit exactly one lock.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片按一把锁精确切好的金属。

branches.en: THE DOOR: the bolt slides back with one turn.
branches.cn: 门这条线：一拧，锁舌就缩回去。

branches.en: THE ANSWER: the one element that makes it work.
branches.cn: 答案这条线：让一切成立的那一个要素。

branches.en: THE TEXTBOOK: a list of answers at the back.
branches.cn: 教辅这条线：书后的答案表。

branches.en: THE DESK: fingers on a keyboard, data going in.
branches.cn: 桌面这条线：手指在键盘上录入数据。

branches.en: THE SCALE: a home note the melody returns to.
branches.cn: 音阶这条线：旋律总要回到的主音。

intro.en: Key is a native word; compounds and English endings do the whole job.
intro.cn: key 是本族词，复合与英语词尾包办全部构词。

latinIntro.en: Key has no Latin root, so the list below stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: key 没有拉丁词根，因此下面留空。

definition_zh: 键盘；（乐器的）键盘；用键盘输入
definition_en: the set of keys on a computer, typewriter, or musical instrument, or to enter data using such keys
core_image: 一整片排列整齐的方键，中间那行有一条微微磨亮的横道
scene: 深夜书桌前，屏幕的光照着摊开的双手，指尖在方格里起落。He wiped crumbs off the keyboard before starting work.
sceneCN: 这里 keyboard 是「键盘」（第 1 个义项：电脑或打字机上的一整排按键），句意为他开始工作前把键盘上的碎屑擦掉。画面里的物件：书桌、屏幕光、双手。

derivatives.zh: 由 keyboard 加 -ist 构成，指键盘手
由 keyboard 加 -ing 构成，指键盘录入技能
构成词根，指单个按键或钥匙

senses.title: The keys of a computer
senses.definition: the set of letter, number, and function keys used to enter data
senses.definitionCN: 用来输入数据的字母、数字和功能键的总和
senses.example: The laptop keyboard is smaller than a desk one.
senses.exampleCN: 笔记本键盘比台式机的要小。
senses.why: The panel sense is the base layer: keys set into one board.
senses.whyCN: 面板义是基础层：按键装在同一块板上。

senses.title: The keys of a musical instrument
senses.definition: the row of black and white keys on a piano, organ, or synthesizer
senses.definitionCN: 钢琴、风琴或电子琴上的黑白琴键
senses.example: She learned the piano before she touched a keyboard.
senses.exampleCN: 她在弹电子琴之前先学了钢琴。
senses.why: Organs and pianos put the same board of keys under the hands.
senses.whyCN: 风琴和钢琴把同样的一块键板放在手下。

senses.title: An electronic instrument
senses.definition: an electronic instrument played with keys, especially in a band
senses.definitionCN: 用键盘演奏的电子乐器，尤指乐队里的那种
senses.example: The band has drums, bass, and keyboard.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队有鼓、贝斯和键盘。
senses.why: An instrument named after its panel is a short step from the panel itself.
senses.whyCN: 以面板命名的乐器，离面板本身只有一步。

senses.title: The typing skill
senses.definition: the skill or activity of typing on a keyboard
senses.definitionCN: 在键盘上打字的技能或活动
senses.example: Keyboarding is taught in the first year.
senses.exampleCN: 第一年就教键盘录入。
senses.why: A skill named after the tool shows how central the keyboard became.
senses.whyCN: 以工具命名一项技能，说明键盘有多核心。

senses.title: To enter data by keys
senses.definition: to input text or numbers using a keyboard
senses.definitionCN: 使用键盘输入文字或数字
senses.example: The forms were keyboarded overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 这些表格是一夜之间录进去的。
senses.why: The verb simply turns the noun into the action of using it.
senses.whyCN: 动词只是把名词变成使用它的动作。

intro.en: Keyboard is an English compound of key and board, built when keys were set into one panel.
intro.cn: keyboard 是 key 与 board 的英语复合词，在按键被装进同一块面板时才造出来。

items.en: cǣg, key, was the native word for a lock opener.
items.cn: cǣg 是本族词，指开锁的钥匙。

items.en: bord meant a plank, table, or flat surface.
items.cn: bord 意为木板、桌面或平面。

items.en: The compound named the row of keys on an organ in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 十七世纪时这个复合词指风琴上的琴键排。

items.en: Typewriters carried the word to machines for writing in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 十九世纪打字机把词义带到书写机器上。

items.en: Computers fixed the modern sense of the panel in front of the screen.
items.cn: 计算机固定了屏幕前那块面板的现代义。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the key family; the near-meaning group holds other input and musical terms.
note.cn: 形近组收 key 词族；近义组收其他输入与乐器术语。

entries.definition: One button, or a lock opener.
entries.definitionCN: 构成词根，指单个按键或钥匙。

entries.definition: A small set of keys, as on a phone.
entries.definitionCN: 相似复合词，指电话等的小键盘。

entries.definition: The opening for a key.
entries.definitionCN: 相似复合词，指锁孔。

entries.definition: A machine with keys that prints letters.
entries.definitionCN: 指带键盘的打字机。

entries.definition: A large keyboard instrument with strings.
entries.definitionCN: 指钢琴，键盘乐器的代表。

entries.definition: The display surface next to a keyboard.
entries.definitionCN: 指屏幕，与键盘相邻。

normalIntro.en: These hooks run from a plank with keys to the worn shine on the middle row.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从装着按键的木板走到中间那行磨亮的痕迹。

normal.en: Keyboard is simply key plus board, a board of keys.
normal.cn: keyboard 就是 key 加 board，一块放键的板。

normal.en: Board was the old word for a plank or table.
normal.cn: board 原指木板或桌子。

normal.en: A keyboardist plays the keyboard in a band.
normal.cn: keyboardist 是在乐队里弹键盘的人。

normal.en: Keyboard shortcuts save the fingers a trip to the mouse.
normal.cn: 键盘快捷键让手不必去碰鼠标。

normal.en: The organ had a keyboard before the typewriter did.
normal.cn: 风琴上的键盘比打字机上出现得更早。

abstract.en: A keyboard is a field of small squares you touch in order.
abstract.cn: 键盘是一片要按顺序触碰的小方格。

abstract.en: Every key is a word waiting to be chosen.
abstract.cn: 每个键都是一个等着被选中的字。

abstract.en: The worn middle row shows where thoughts pass most.
abstract.cn: 磨亮的中间一行说明思绪最爱从这里过。

examples.en: She spilled tea on the keyboard again.
examples.cn: 她又把茶洒在键盘上了。

examples.en: The keyboard on this laptop is very quiet.
examples.cn: 这台笔记本的键盘很安静。

examples.en: He keyboarded the whole list in one evening.
examples.cn: 他一晚上把整份清单录了进去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ki 板」—— 一块放满了键的板，就是键盘

root: 古英语 cǣg「钥匙」+ bord「木板、桌面」→ 英语复合词 keyboard，十七世纪指风琴键盘，后指打字机与电脑键盘。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: computer keys, instrument keys, the electronic instrument, the typing skill, and the verb for keying data.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：电脑键盘、乐器键盘、电子键盘乐器、键盘录入技能，以及键入数据的动词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one panel holding a hundred small keys in rows.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块面板上成排装着一百来个小键。

branches.en: THE DESK: letters going in and words coming out.
branches.cn: 书桌这条线：字母进去，词出来。

branches.en: THE PIANO: black and white keys in order.
branches.cn: 钢琴这条线：黑白琴键排成行。

branches.en: THE BAND: a player behind two rows of keys.
branches.cn: 乐队这条线：两排键后面的乐手。

branches.en: THE LAPTOP: a small panel folded on a hinge.
branches.cn: 笔记本这条线：折在铰链上的小面板。

branches.en: THE CLASSROOM: fingers drilled into speed.
branches.cn: 教室这条线：练到熟练的手指。

intro.en: Keyboard is a two-part English compound; the family grows with English endings.
intro.cn: keyboard 是两部分组成的英语复合词，词族靠英语词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: No Latin root is involved here, so the list below stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词根，因此下面留空。

definition_zh: 踢；踢球；踢腿；戒除（习惯）；刺激；乐趣
definition_en: to hit something with the foot, or to end a habit, usually with effort
core_image: 一只脚猛地抬起，鞋尖撞在球面上，球飞了出去
scene: 球场边风很冷，少年把球抛起，抬腿一脚，球穿过整片草地。He kicked the ball over the fence and climbed after it.
sceneCN: 这里 kick 是「踢」（第 1 个义项：用脚击打），句意为他把球踢过篱笆，又爬过去捡。画面里的物件：球场、草地、篱笆。

pos.zh: 动词：踢；踢球；戒除；（枪）后坐

derivatives.zh: 由 kick 加 -er 构成，指踢球的人或（美式足球）踢球员
由 kick 加 -ing 构成，义为「活泼的；带劲的」

senses.title: To hit with the foot
senses.definition: to strike something with the foot or feet
senses.definitionCN: 用一只或两只脚击打某物
senses.example: She kicked the door open with one foot.
senses.exampleCN: 她一脚把门踹开了。
senses.why: The core act is one sudden blow delivered by a leg.
senses.whyCN: 核心动作是腿发出的一记突然打击。

senses.title: To move a ball by foot
senses.definition: to send a ball through the air with the foot, as in a game
senses.definitionCN: 比赛中用脚把球踢出去
senses.example: He kicked the ball straight into the net.
senses.exampleCN: 他直接把球踢进了网里。
senses.why: A ball is the object most often sent away by that blow.
senses.whyCN: 被这一击送走的物件里，球最常见。

senses.title: To thrust a leg
senses.definition: to move the legs sharply, as in swimming or dancing
senses.definitionCN: 在游泳或跳舞中快速蹬腿
senses.example: The baby kicked and laughed in the bath.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿在洗澡水里蹬着腿笑。
senses.why: Legs also kick without hitting anything, as in water.
senses.whyCN: 腿也会空踢，比如在水里。

senses.title: To give up a habit
senses.definition: to stop doing something habitual, often with struggle
senses.definitionCN: 指停止某个习惯，往往经过一番挣扎
senses.example: It took him three tries to kick the smoking habit.
senses.exampleCN: 他试了三次才戒掉抽烟。
senses.why: Giving up a habit is pictured as kicking it away from you.
senses.whyCN: 戒掉习惯被画成把它从身边踢开。

senses.title: A sharp thrill
senses.definition: a feeling of excitement or amusement from something
senses.definitionCN: 从某事得到的兴奋或愉悦
senses.example: She gets a kick out of fixing old bikes.
senses.exampleCN: 她从修旧自行车里得到乐趣。
senses.why: Excitement is a blow felt inside rather than outside.
senses.whyCN: 兴奋是在身体里感到的一记击打。

senses.title: The recoil of a gun
senses.definition: the backward push of a firearm when fired
senses.definitionCN: 枪射击时向后的推力
senses.example: The rifle has a strong kick.
senses.exampleCN: 这把步枪后坐力很大。
senses.why: A gun pushes back exactly where a foot would push.
senses.whyCN: 枪向后推的位置，正是脚会推的位置。

intro.en: Kick is a Middle English word of uncertain origin, probably imitative of the blow it names.
intro.cn: kick 是中古英语词，来源不详，很可能模仿踢击的声音与动作。

items.en: kicken appeared in the fourteenth century meaning to strike with the foot.
items.cn: kicken 十四世纪出现，意为用脚击打。

items.en: No certain source is known; it may echo the sound of a blow.
items.cn: 确切来源不明，可能模仿击打的声音。

items.en: The ball-game sense spread with modern football.
items.cn: 球类比赛的「踢球」义随现代足球传播。

items.en: Kick the habit, meaning to stop, dates from the twentieth century.
items.cn: 表示戒除的 kick the habit 出现于二十世纪。

items.en: The noun kick for excitement grew from drink and sport slang.
items.cn: 表示兴奋的名词义源自饮酒与运动俚语。

note.en: The look-alike group holds short words close in shape; the near-meaning group holds other verbs of striking.
note.cn: 形近组收外形相近的短词；近义组收其他表示击打的动词。

entries.definition: A child, or to tease.
entries.definitionCN: 拼写只差一个字母，义为「小孩；开玩笑」。

entries.definition: The start of a game or event.
entries.definitionCN: 由 kick 加 off 构成，指开球或开始。

entries.definition: One who kicks, as in football.
entries.definitionCN: 由 kick 加 -er 构成，指踢球员。

entries.definition: To hit something hard.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「击打」，语气更普遍。

entries.definition: To drop a ball and kick it before it lands.
entries.definitionCN: 指落下前把球踢出的动作。

entries.definition: To kick something hard, in informal British use.
entries.definitionCN: 英式口语里指狠狠地踢。

normalIntro.en: These hooks run from a foot striking a ball to the recoil of a rifle.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从脚踢中球走到步枪的后坐。

normal.en: Kick is probably imitative, echoing the impact itself.
normal.cn: kick 很可能是拟声的，模仿撞击本身。

normal.en: Kick off starts a match and also a project.
normal.cn: kick off 既开球，也开启一个项目。

normal.en: Kick the habit means to stop for good.
normal.cn: kick the habit 指彻底戒掉。

normal.en: Get a kick out of means enjoy it a great deal.
normal.cn: get a kick out of 指从其中得到很大乐趣。

normal.en: Kicked is the past form; there is no kickt.
normal.cn: 过去式是 kicked，没有 kickt。

abstract.en: A kick is a sudden decision made with the foot.
abstract.cn: 踢是用脚做出的一个突然决定。

abstract.en: The same word shakes off a ball and shakes off a habit.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能踢开球，也能甩掉习惯。

abstract.en: Excitement and recoil are both a backward push.
abstract.cn: 刺激与后坐都是一种向后的推力。

examples.en: He kicked the empty can down the street.
examples.cn: 他一路踢着空罐子。

examples.en: The match kicks off at three.
examples.cn: 比赛三点开球。

examples.en: She finally kicked the habit last winter.
examples.cn: 去年冬天她终于戒掉了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「踢克」—— 一腿踢过去，克住对方

root: 中古英语 kicken「用脚击打」，来源不详，疑为拟声词；现代由足球与俚语扩展出「开球、戒除、刺激」等义。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses: kicking with the foot, kicking a ball, thrusting a leg, giving up a habit, a thrill, and the recoil of a gun.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项：用脚踢、踢球、蹬腿、戒除习惯、刺激乐趣，以及枪的后坐力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foot snapping forward into whatever is in front of it.
core.cn: 核心意象：脚猛地向前打中眼前的东西。

branches.en: THE DOOR: one foot and it swings open.
branches.cn: 门这条线：一脚过去，门就开了。

branches.en: THE FIELD: a ball sent over the grass.
branches.cn: 球场这条线：球飞过草地。

branches.en: THE BATH: small legs working in water.
branches.cn: 浴缸这条线：水里蹬个不停的小腿。

branches.en: THE LAST CIGARETTE: kicking a habit away.
branches.cn: 最后一支烟这条线：把习惯踢掉。

branches.en: THE SHOULDER: a push back from the thing you hit.
branches.cn: 肩膀这条线：打中的东西回推你。

intro.en: Kick is a native verb with an uncertain root; English endings build the rest.

definition_zh: 小孩；孩子；小山羊；小山羊皮；（口语）开玩笑；哄骗
definition_en: a child, or a young goat, or to say something untrue as a joke
core_image: 一只小山羊跟在母羊后面，蹦两下停一下
scene: 院子里两只小山羊绕着母亲转圈，见人来了就往后退半步。The kids were still playing outside when it got dark.
sceneCN: 这里 kid 是「小孩」（第 1 个义项：口语里的孩子），句意为天黑时孩子们还在外面玩。画面里的物件：院子、天黑、玩耍的孩子。

pos.zh: 名词：小孩；孩子；小山羊；小山羊皮

collocations.zh: 小山羊皮手套；温和对待

derivatives.zh: 由 kid 加 -ie 构成，口语里指小孩
由 kid 加 nap 加 -er 构成，指绑匪（原意为偷小孩的人）
形近词，指肾，与 kid 无关

senses.title: A child, in informal speech
senses.definition: a young person, used in friendly or casual talk
senses.definitionCN: 在亲切或随便的说话中称呼年幼的人
senses.example: The kids ran to the door when the bell rang.
senses.exampleCN: 门铃一响，孩子们就跑到门口。
senses.why: The everyday sense is the young of the family, said with affection.
senses.whyCN: 日常义指家里的小的一辈，带亲切感。

senses.title: A young goat
senses.definition: a young goat, the oldest sense of the word
senses.definitionCN: 幼年的山羊，是这个词最古老的义
senses.example: Two kids stayed close to the nanny goat.
senses.exampleCN: 两只小山羊紧跟着母羊。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a young goat, and it keeps the word animal-based.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义是小山羊，让这个词始终带着动物底色。

senses.title: Leather from a young goat
senses.definition: soft leather made from the skin of a young goat
senses.definitionCN: 用小山羊皮制成的柔软皮革
senses.example: The gloves are made of kid.
senses.exampleCN: 这副手套是小山羊皮做的。
senses.why: The hide of that animal became a byword for soft leather.
senses.whyCN: 那种动物的皮成了柔软皮革的代称。

senses.title: To tease someone playfully
senses.definition: to say something untrue in fun, or to tease gently
senses.definitionCN: 为好玩说不真实的话，或轻轻打趣
senses.example: I am only kidding; the exam is next week.
senses.exampleCN: 我只是开玩笑，考试在下周。
senses.why: Teasing is playful pretending, like a young goat butting for fun.
senses.whyCN: 打趣是好玩的假装，像小山羊闹着顶人。

senses.title: To deceive as a joke
senses.definition: to make someone believe something untrue, often lightly
senses.definitionCN: 使某人相信不实之事，多为轻松性质
senses.example: They kidded him into thinking the meeting was cancelled.
senses.exampleCN: 他们哄他以为会议取消了。
senses.why: The deception is light: the other person is meant to laugh, not lose.
senses.whyCN: 这种哄骗很轻：对方该笑，而不是吃亏。

senses.title: A young animal of some species
senses.definition: the young of certain animals, as in a fox kid
senses.definitionCN: 某些动物的幼崽，如小狐狸
senses.example: The keeper fed the fox kid by hand.
senses.exampleCN: 饲养员亲手喂那只小狐狸。
senses.why: Other species keep the same young-animal pattern.
senses.whyCN: 其他物种也沿用同样的「幼崽」说法。

intro.en: Kid comes from Old Norse kith, a young goat, and the child sense is a later informal extension.
intro.cn: kid 来自古北欧语 kith「小山羊」，指孩子是后来口语化的引申。

items.en: kith named a young goat and entered northern English dialects.
items.cn: kith 指小山羊，进入英格兰北部方言。

items.en: The goat sense was standard and gave kid gloves from its leather.
items.cn: 中古英语里「小山羊」是标准义，其皮革做成 kid gloves。

items.en: The child sense came from slang for a young person in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 指孩子的义来自十七世纪指年轻人的俚语。

items.en: The verb sense of joking grew in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 开玩笑的动词义在十九世纪发展起来。

items.en: The child sense now dominates everyday speech.
items.cn: 如今日常口语里「孩子」义占主导。

note.en: The look-alike group holds short words close in shape; the near-meaning group holds other words for children and goats.
note.cn: 形近组收外形相近的短词；近义组收其他表示孩子与山羊的词。

entries.definition: An organ that filters blood.
entries.definitionCN: 拼写开头相同，指肾，与 kid 无关。

entries.definition: The -ing form of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词的 -ing 形式，义为「开玩笑」。

entries.definition: A child, in very informal use.
entries.definitionCN: 口语派生词，指小孩。

entries.definition: The neutral word for a young person.
entries.definitionCN: 最中性的「孩子」。

entries.definition: The adult animal.
entries.definitionCN: 指成年的山羊。

entries.definition: An informal word for a young person.
entries.definitionCN: 较口语的「年轻人」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a small goat to the joke told after an exam.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一只小山羊走到考完试后的一句玩笑。

normal.en: The goat sense is the oldest; the child sense is slang that won.
normal.cn: 山羊义最古老，孩子义是笑到最后的俚语。

normal.en: Just kidding is the everyday way to cancel a joke.
normal.cn: just kidding 是取消玩笑的日常说法。

normal.en: Kid gloves come from soft goat leather.
normal.cn: kid gloves 原本来自柔软的小山羊皮。

normal.en: Kidnapper once meant a stealer of children.
normal.cn: kidnapper 原意是偷小孩的人。

normal.en: Kidney looks like kid but is a different word.
normal.cn: kidney 看着像 kid，但是另一个词。

abstract.en: A kid is a young thing that has not yet learned to stand still.
abstract.cn: 小孩就是还站不住的小东西。

abstract.en: The same word is a goat, a child, and a joke.
abstract.cn: 同一个词可以是山羊、孩子，也可以是一句玩笑。

abstract.en: Tenderness is what goat leather and children share.
abstract.cn: 柔软是山羊皮与孩子共有的特点。

examples.en: The kids are playing in the yard.
examples.cn: 孩子们在院子里玩。

examples.en: Are you kidding about moving abroad?
examples.cn: 你说要搬去国外是开玩笑吧？

examples.en: A kid was born on the farm last night.
examples.cn: 昨晚农场里出生了一只小山羊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「kid 是小子」—— 小鬼头，就是小孩

root: 古北欧语 kith「小山羊」→ 北部英语方言 kid「小山羊；小山羊皮」→ 十七世纪俚语「年轻人」→ 现代口语「孩子」，另生出「开玩笑」动词义。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses: a child, a young goat, goat leather, playful teasing, light deception, and the young of some animals.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项：孩子、小山羊、小山羊皮、打趣、轻哄，以及某种动物的幼崽。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a young goat trotting behind its mother.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只跟在母羊后面的小山羊。

branches.en: THE YARD: children shouting before dark.
branches.cn: 院子这条线：天黑前还在喊叫的孩子。

branches.en: THE FARM: a small goat and its soft hide.
branches.cn: 农场这条线：小山羊与柔软的皮。

branches.en: THE PLAYGROUND: teasing that is not meant to hurt.
branches.cn: 操场这条线：不带恶意的打趣。

branches.en: THE ZOO: the young of another species.
branches.cn: 动物园这条线：别的物种的幼崽。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: the word parents use half-jokingly.
branches.cn: 家庭这条线：父母半开玩笑用的称呼。

intro.en: Kid is a borrowed short noun; English endings and compounds do the rest.
intro.cn: kid 是借来的短名词，其余由英语词尾与复合构成。

latinIntro.en: Kid has no Latin root, so the Latin column stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: kid 没有拉丁词根，因此拉丁一栏留空。

definition_zh: 杀死；弄死；毁掉；消磨（时间）；使痛苦
definition_en: to cause the death of a living thing, and by extension to end, ruin, or use up something such as time or a feeling
core_image: 一击落下，原本还在动的东西彻底静止
scene: 巷子里那只被撞伤的猫躺在墙根，谁都下不了手。No one in the yard had the heart to kill the injured bird, so they called a vet instead.
sceneCN: 这里 kill 是「杀死、弄死」（第 1 个义项：使活物死亡），句意是院里没人忍心弄死那只受伤的小鸟，于是打电话叫了兽医。背景是墙根、受伤的小动物和一部电话。

collocations.phrase: kill two birds with one stone

derivatives.zh: kill 加 -er 构成，指杀人者或致命之物
kill 加 -ing 构成，指杀害行为，口语中也指「赚了一大笔」
kill 与 joy 合成的复合词，指扫兴的人
over 与 kill 合成，原指火力过剩，今指做得过头

senses.title: To take the life of a living thing
senses.definition: to cause the death of a person, animal, or plant
senses.definitionCN: 使某人、某动物或某植物死亡
senses.example: The frost killed the young shoots overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 霜冻一夜之间冻死了嫩芽。
senses.why: The oldest sense rests on a simple physical picture: a blow that ends all movement.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项基于一个简单的画面：一击下去，一切动静都停止了。

senses.title: To end something as if by a blow
senses.definition: to destroy or bring an end to something non-living, such as a plan or a hope
senses.definitionCN: 使计划、希望等非生物的事物毁灭或终止
senses.example: One careless remark killed the whole idea.
senses.exampleCN: 一句随口的话就把整个想法扼杀了。
senses.why: Because the literal act ends life, the word readily transfers to anything that stops growing.
senses.whyCN: 因为本义是终止生命，这个词很自然就挪用到任何停止生长的事物上。

senses.title: To use up time
senses.definition: to pass time while waiting, especially in a way that fills the empty hours
senses.definitionCN: 在等待时把空闲的时间打发过去
senses.example: We killed an hour at the station by counting trains.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在车站数着列车，消磨了一个小时。
senses.why: Empty time feels like something to be got rid of, so the word for ending life serves for ending boredom.
senses.whyCN: 空白的时间像是要处理掉的东西，于是表示结束生命的词也用来结束无聊。

senses.title: To cause great pain
senses.definition: to hurt someone badly, especially through emotion rather than force
senses.definitionCN: 多指在情感上把人伤害得极重，而非用武力
senses.example: His silence killed me more than any shouting.
senses.exampleCN: 他的沉默比任何喊叫都更让我难受。
senses.why: When pain is extreme it is described as the worst the body can bear, so the strongest word for ending is borrowed for suffering.
senses.whyCN: 痛苦到了极点就被说成身体能承受的极限，于是表示终结的最强词被借来表示难受。

senses.title: To stop a machine or engine
senses.definition: to switch off an engine or a device
senses.definitionCN: 把发动机或设备关掉
senses.example: Kill the engine before you check the oil.
senses.exampleCN: 检查机油之前先熄火。
senses.why: An engine that stops is dead in miniature, so drivers say they kill it.
senses.whyCN: 停下来的发动机就像小规模地死掉，所以司机说把它关掉。

senses.title: To defeat completely
senses.definition: to beat an opponent so thoroughly that the contest is over
senses.definitionCN: 把对手打败到比赛立刻失去悬念
senses.example: The away team killed the game in the first half.
senses.exampleCN: 客队在上半场就让比赛失去悬念。
senses.why: In sport, ending the contest feels like killing its chances, so the word names total dominance.
senses.whyCN: 在体育里，终结比赛的悬念就像把机会杀掉，于是这个词用来指完全的压制。

senses.title: To cancel or remove a story
senses.definition: to drop a piece of news or a planned piece of work before it appears
senses.definitionCN: 在新闻或稿件发表之前把它撤掉不用
senses.example: The editor killed the interview at the last minute.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑在最后一刻把访谈稿撤了下来。
senses.why: In newsrooms the act of striking a story from the page was called killing it, and the usage stayed.
senses.whyCN: 在编辑部里把稿子从版面上划掉被称作杀掉稿件，这种说法沿用至今。

senses.title: To process a drug or germ
senses.definition: to destroy germs, or to weaken a drug so that it can no longer be active
senses.definitionCN: 消灭细菌，或使药物失去活性
senses.example: Boiling the water kills most of the bacteria.
senses.exampleCN: 把水烧开能杀死大部分细菌。
senses.why: The medical sense keeps the original image: a living agent is made inoperative.
senses.whyCN: 医学义保留了原本的画面：让活的因子失去作用。

senses.title: The animal killed in hunting
senses.definition: an animal that has been hunted and killed, especially in sport
senses.definitionCN: 狩猎中打到的猎物，尤指运动狩猎所得
senses.example: The hounds brought down a fine kill.
senses.exampleCN: 猎犬包抄下一头不错的猎物。
senses.why: The verb turned into a noun by naming the result of its own action, a common path in English.
senses.whyCN: 动词直接名词化，指自己行为的结果，这是英语里常见的一条路。

intro.en: Kill is a Middle English word whose roots are uncertain; it is not related to Latin occidere, and the common guess about a Latin origin has no solid support.
intro.cn: kill 是中古英语词，词根来源不确定；它与拉丁语 occidere 无关，常见的那种拉丁来源猜测缺乏可靠证据。

items.en: The verb appears as killen in Middle English, first in northern texts.
items.cn: 这个动词在中古英语中写作 killen，最早见于北部地区的文本。

items.en: Its earliest recorded use concerns striking or beating, with dying as a result.
items.cn: 它最早的记录用法是打、击，结果是死亡。

items.en: No agreed source has been found; a link with Old English cwellan is often suggested but not proved.
items.cn: 至今未找到公认的来源；常有人提出与古英语 cwellan 有关，但未得到证实。

items.en: The plain sense ending life is fixed in English from the sixteenth century onwards.
items.cn: 表示结束生命的直白义项从十六世纪起在英语中固定下来。

items.en: The extended senses of ruining a plan, passing time, and switching off a machine all grow from that plain sense.
items.cn: 毁掉计划、打发时间、关掉机器等引申义都从这一直白义项生长出来。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that are spelled or sounded close to kill; the near-meaning group holds stronger and weaker ways of saying the same act.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写或读音接近 kill 的词；近义组收同一行为的更重与更轻的说法。

entries.definition: The same ending with a different first letter, naming raised ground.
entries.definitionCN: 只差首字母的拼写近邻，指小山，词源与 kill 无关。

entries.definition: A silent letter makes kiln look like kill plus n, but it is a baking oven.
entries.definitionCN: 多一个不发音的字母，看起来像 kill 加 n，其实指烧窑。

entries.definition: One letter away, naming the pleated Scottish skirt.
entries.definitionCN: 只差一个字母，指苏格兰褶裙。

entries.definition: A spelling in some old glossaries for a small stream, unrelated and obsolete.
entries.definitionCN: 某个旧词表里的拼写，指小溪，与 kill 无关且已废弃。

entries.definition: To kill a person unlawfully and with intent.
entries.definitionCN: 指非法且有预谋地杀人，是法律用语。

entries.definition: To kill, used mostly of heroes and dragons in old stories.
entries.definitionCN: 指杀死，多用于旧故事里的英雄与恶龙。

entries.definition: To kill a sick animal humanely.
entries.definitionCN: 指为结束痛苦而人道地杀死患病动物。

entries.definition: To injure without causing death.
entries.definitionCN: 指伤害而未致死，与 kill 的结果相反。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from the plain act to the many things people say they kill besides creatures.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从最直白的动作出发，走到人们说被 kill 掉的、动物以外的种种东西。

normal.en: Kill takes -s, -ed, and -ing without any stem change.
normal.cn: kill 变三单、过去式、现在分词都不改词干。

normal.en: Kill time literally makes the clock feel dead.
normal.cn: kill time 就是把钟面上的时间弄死。

normal.en: The -er ending gives killer, the one who does it.
normal.cn: 加 -er 得到 killer，指做这件事的人。

normal.en: One shot, two birds: the proverb packs the whole word.
normal.cn: 一箭双雕的谚语把这个词的全部用法都装了进去。

normal.en: Kill the engine is the everyday mechanical sense.
normal.cn: kill the engine 是日常里的机械用法。

abstract.en: A struck match: the tiny flame goes out in a blink, and the smallest moment of death is the word itself.
abstract.cn: 划着又熄灭的火柴：小火苗一眨眼就没，死亡最小的那一瞬就是这个词。

abstract.en: An empty afternoon is a stretch of clock to be used up, so people speak of killing it.
abstract.cn: 空荡荡的下午是一段等着被用完的时钟，所以人们说要 killing it。

abstract.en: A word killed in an editor's room never reaches print, yet it still dies.
abstract.cn: 被编辑在屋里撤掉的稿子从没见报，可它照样死过一次。

examples.en: Too much rain can kill a young crop.
examples.cn: 雨水太多会把幼苗淹死。

examples.en: She killed the lights before leaving the studio.
examples.cn: 她离开工作室前把灯关了。

examples.en: We killed the whole afternoon arguing about a name.
examples.cn: 我们为一个名字争了整个下午。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「剋」——剋死，古书里的字正好握住了这个词的狠劲

root: 中古英语 killen，最早记录的是「打、击」而致死；来源不确定，或有与古英语 cwellan（杀）相关的可能，但未证实；十六世纪起固定为「结束生命」，并引申出毁掉、消磨、关掉等义。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses: the plain act of ending life, then the ending of plans, hours, pain, engines, contests, stories, and germs, and finally the hunted animal itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项：先是结束生命的直白动作，接着是结束计划、时间、痛苦、机器、悬念、稿件与细菌，最后是以动词结果命名的猎物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one blow, and the thing that was moving stops for good.
core.cn: 核心意象：一击落下，原本还在动的东西彻底停住。

branches.en: THE BLOW LINE: a strike ends a living thing, from animals to germs.
branches.cn: 打击这条线：一击结束一个活物，从动物到细菌。

branches.en: THE ENDING LINE: anything that stops growing is spoken of as killed, even hope or a story.
branches.cn: 终结这条线：任何停止生长的东西都被说成被杀，包括希望和稿子。

branches.en: THE CLOCK LINE: empty time is used up as if it were alive.
branches.cn: 时钟这条线：空白的时间像活物一样被用掉。

branches.en: THE PRESSURE LINE: extreme pain and total defeat both borrow the strongest word.
branches.cn: 压力这条线：极度的痛和彻底的胜都借用这个最重的词。

branches.en: THE SWITCH LINE: an engine that stops is a small death.
branches.cn: 开关这条线：停下来的发动机就是一次小死亡。

intro.en: Kill is a short native verb that builds mostly by compounding, so the items below are the small set of words English made from it.
intro.cn: kill 是一个短小的本土动词，主要靠合成造词，下面的条目是英语由它构成的少数词。

latinIntro.en: Kill has no Latin ancestry, so the Latin-looking forms below are offered only as contrasts to the real word family.
latinIntro.cn: kill 没有拉丁血统，下面这些看似拉丁的形式只是与真实词族的对照。

items.example: One fall killed the old tree.
items.exampleCN: 一次倒伏弄死了那棵老树。

items.example: The killing of the wolf ended the attacks.
items.exampleCN: 打死那只狼之后袭击就停了。

items.meaning: a person or thing that kills
items.example: Heart disease is a leading killer.
The killjoy closed the party early.
items.exampleCN: 那个扫兴的人早早结束了聚会。

items.example: Two guards for one door is overkill.
items.exampleCN: 一扇门配两个守卫实在过头。
乌鸦聚在被撞死的动物上方。
它把 kill 变成 killer。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉丁语「打倒、杀死」，与 kill 只是意义相近，并非同源
拉丁语「砍、击倒」，为拉丁系杀伐词的根，与 kill 无词源关系

definition_zh: 千米；公里
definition_en: a unit of distance equal to one thousand metres, used for roads, journeys, and maps
core_image: 公路边一块写着距某城若干公里的白色路牌
scene: 黄昏的省道上，路边立着指示里程的白牌。The sign said the next town was eight kilometres away, so we kept walking.
sceneCN: 这里 kilometre 是「千米、公里」（第 1 个义项：距离单位，等于一千米），句意是牌子上说下一个镇还有八公里，于是他们继续走。画面里有黄昏、省道和白色路牌。

pos.zh: 千米（口语中作为一整段距离）

derivatives.zh: 截短形式，口语里也可泛指「一公里」或「一公斤」
kilometre 的基本单位，源自希腊语的「量度」
kilometre 加 -ic 构成的形容词，指以公里计的，多用于书面
与 kilometre 同一义场的里程计算说法，由 mile 加 -age 构成

senses.title: A unit of distance of a thousand metres
senses.definition: a metric unit of length equal to one thousand metres
senses.definitionCN: 公制长度单位，等于一千米
senses.example: The lake is three kilometres across.
senses.exampleCN: 这个湖宽三公里。
senses.why: The name is a compound of thousand and metre, so the unit explains its own size.
senses.whyCN: 名字本身就是「千」加「米」的复合，单位自己在解释大小。

senses.title: Distance written on signs and maps
senses.definition: the unit used to state the distance between places
senses.definitionCN: 用来说明两地之间距离的单位
senses.example: Every kilometre is marked on the map.
senses.exampleCN: 地图上每一公里都标了出来。
senses.why: The word takes on a mapping sense because roads and charts must state distances in one shared unit.
senses.whyCN: 公路和地图必须用同一个单位写明距离，于是这个词带上了制图意义。

senses.title: A measure of speed
senses.definition: the unit in which speed is stated as kilometres per hour
senses.definitionCN: 以每小时公里数表示速度时的单位
senses.example: The limit here is fifty kilometres an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的限速是每小时五十公里。
senses.why: Speed is distance over time, so a distance unit naturally appears in every speed limit.
senses.whyCN: 速度是距离除以时间，所以每个限速牌上都自然出现距离单位。

senses.title: A measure of area
senses.definition: the unit squared, used for land and large surfaces
senses.definitionCN: 平方之后用来量土地和大面积
senses.example: The park covers forty square kilometres.
senses.exampleCN: 这座公园占地四十平方公里。
senses.why: Once a length unit exists, squaring it gives the unit for land, and the word simply doubles up.
senses.whyCN: 长度单位一确立，平方一下就得到土地单位的说法，这个词只是叠加使用。

senses.title: A stretch of distance in speech
senses.definition: a loose way of naming a short distance, as in the last kilometre of a race
senses.definitionCN: 口语里指一小段路程，如赛跑的最后一段
senses.example: He pulled ahead in the final kilometre.
senses.exampleCN: 他在最后一公里拉开了距离。
senses.why: Once the word means a stretch of road, the last stretch of a race can be named in it without any measuring.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词指一段路，赛跑的最后一段就可以用它来称呼，而不必真的去量。

intro.en: Kilometre is a French-built modern word: a Greek prefix for thousand joined to a French unit of length.
intro.cn: kilometre 是法国人造的现代词：希腊语表示「千」的前缀接上法语长度单位。

items.en: The prefix comes from khilioi, Greek for a thousand.
items.cn: 前缀来自希腊语 khilioi，意为一千。

items.en: The base comes from metron, meaning measure.
items.cn: 词基本自 metron，意为「量度」。

items.en: French scientists coined metre as a unit of length in the late eighteenth century.
items.cn: 十八世纪末法国科学家造出 metre 作为长度单位。

items.en: Kilometre was formed on the same pattern for a thousand metres.
items.cn: kilometre 按同一模式造成，指一千米。

items.en: English took the word in the nineteenth century and later shortened the ending to kilometer in American use.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪引入，美国后来把词尾缩成 kilometer。

note.en: The look-alike group holds units built with the same Greek prefix; the near-meaning group holds older and non-metric measures of distance.
note.cn: 形近组收用同一希腊前缀构成的单位；近义组收更早的和非公制的距离单位。

entries.definition: A thousand grams, the same pattern applied to mass.
entries.definitionCN: 一千克，同一模式用在质量上。

entries.definition: A thousand watts, the same pattern applied to power.
entries.definitionCN: 一千瓦，同一模式用在功率上。

entries.definition: The unit to which the prefix thousand is attached.
entries.definitionCN: 被加上「千」这个前缀的基本单位。

entries.definition: A thousandth of a metre, the same unit with a smaller prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 一毫米，同一单位配更小的前缀。

entries.definition: An imperial distance of about one and six tenths kilometres.
entries.definitionCN: 英制距离，约一点六公里，与公里并用时常需换算。

entries.definition: The metric base unit of length.
entries.definitionCN: 公制的基本长度单位。

entries.definition: A short imperial length of about ninety centimetres.
entries.definitionCN: 英制短长度，约九十厘米。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the word to roads, speed limits, and the two languages that built it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把词绑在公路、限速和造出它的两种语言上。

normal.en: Kilo- means a thousand and metre means measure.
normal.cn: kilo- 意为千，metre 意为量度。

normal.en: The British write metre, the Americans write meter.
normal.cn: 英式写 metre，美式写 meter。

normal.en: Speed limits pair it with hour: kilometres per hour.
normal.cn: 限速牌把它和小时配对：每小时公里。

normal.en: Square it and it measures land.
normal.cn: 平方之后就用来量土地。

normal.en: Km on a road sign always stands for this word.
normal.cn: 路牌上的 km 永远代表这个词。

abstract.en: A kilometre is a thousand footsteps of the same length put end to end.
abstract.cn: 一公里就是把一千个等长的脚步首尾接起来。

abstract.en: Road signs turn the word into a promise about how much walking is left.
abstract.cn: 路牌把这个词变成一句承诺：还剩多少路要走。

abstract.en: One unit shared by every country means nobody has to convert at the border.
abstract.cn: 各国共用一种单位，意味着过境不必换算。

examples.en: The village is two kilometres from the sea.
examples.cn: 这个村子离海两公里。

examples.en: She runs ten kilometres every Sunday morning.
examples.cn: 她每个周日早上跑十公里。

examples.en: Prices are listed per kilometre of transport.
examples.cn: 运费按每公里列价。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「kilometre」前半像「开了米」—— 开了一千米就是一公里

root: 由希腊语 khilioi（千）与 metron（量度）经法语复合而成，metre 为十八世纪末法国制定的长度单位，kilometre 即其后按同一模式造出的「千米」。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: the unit itself, distance on signs and maps, speed, area, and a loose spoken stretch of road.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：单位本身、路牌与地图上的距离、速度、面积，以及口语里一段路。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thousand strides laid end to end along a measured line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一千步等长的脚步沿一条量好的线首尾相接。

branches.en: THE SIGN LINE: the unit fixed on plates and maps.
branches.cn: 路牌这条线：单位被固定在牌子和地图上。

branches.en: THE SPEED LINE: distance per hour.
branches.cn: 速度这条线：每小时走多远。

branches.en: THE LAND LINE: the same unit squared for surfaces.
branches.cn: 土地这条线：同一单位平方之后量面积。

branches.en: THE RACE LINE: the last stretch that decides a run.
branches.cn: 赛程这条线：决定胜负的最后一段。

branches.en: THE TRAVEL LINE: every journey is counted in these units.
branches.cn: 旅程这条线：每一段路都用它来计数。

intro.en: The word is a compound whose pieces are all still working: a prefix, a base, a plural ending, and a two-letter symbol.
intro.cn: 这是个复合词，各部分至今都在使用：一个前缀、一个词基、一个复数词尾和两个字母的符号。

latinIntro.en: The parts came through Greek and French, so the entries below are Greek and French forms rather than native Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 构词成分经由希腊语和法语而来，下面的条目是希腊语与法语形式，而非本土拉丁语。

items.example: It is one kilometre to the bridge.
Ten kilometres is a long walk.
The room is four metres wide.

items.exampleCN: 图表里全是以公里计的距离。

definition_zh: 种类；一类；同类的
definition_en: a group of things that share the same nature, and the adjective meaning belonging to the same group
core_image: 一群长得一模一样的东西被归到同一个小篮子里
scene: 书店掌柜把架上的书按题材分门别类码好。She likes this kind of story and reads one every week.
sceneCN: 这里 kind 是「种类」（第 1 个义项：同类事物组成的类别），句意是她喜欢这一类故事，每周读一本。画面里有书架、分类的小牌和一本翻开的书。

pos.zh: 种类；类别；同类的人或物
同类的；属于一类的（较古旧）

derivatives.zh: kind 加 -ly 构成，表示体贴地、好心地
kind 加 -ness 构成，指善意、好心这个性质
古英语词，字面即「同类血亲」，与 kind 同族，指亲族或同类
un- 加 kind 构成，指不厚道的，与「和善」一义对照

senses.title: A class of things sharing a nature
senses.definition: a group whose members share the same qualities
senses.definitionCN: 成员具有相同性质的群体
senses.example: What kind of tea do you prefer?
senses.exampleCN: 你更喜欢哪一种茶？
senses.why: The oldest sense is about birth and stock: things of one kind come from the same origin and so match.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思和出身血统有关：同一种东西同出一源，因此才相像。

senses.title: A person or thing of a sort
senses.definition: a person or thing treated as an example of a sort, often in judgement
senses.definitionCN: 被当作某类例子来评价的人或物
senses.example: He is not the kind to give up easily.
senses.exampleCN: 他不是那种轻易放弃的人。
senses.why: Sorting objects leads naturally to sorting people by character, so the class word becomes a character label.
senses.whyCN: 给物分类很自然就过渡到给人分性格，于是类别词被用来标人。

senses.title: A somewhat way of softening a statement
senses.definition: a spoken modifier meaning somewhat or rather
senses.definitionCN: 口语里表示「有点儿、某种程度上」的修饰语
senses.example: I was kind of tired after the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 旅行结束后我有点累。
senses.why: Placing something vaguely in a kind leaves room for doubt, and that vagueness became a hedge.
senses.whyCN: 把某事含糊地归入某一类就留下了余地，这份含糊后来成了委婉的缓和语。

senses.title: The same nature or family
senses.definition: sharing a common nature, family, or origin, as in kindred
senses.definitionCN: 共享同一性质、家族或来源，如 kindred 里所示
senses.example: They are kind in spirit, if not in blood.
senses.exampleCN: 他们虽无血缘，精神上却是同类。
senses.why: The birth sense survives in fixed phrases where kind still means stock or lineage.
senses.whyCN: 出身义在某些固定说法里留存，那里 kind 仍指血统或家世。

senses.title: A category in trade and law
senses.definition: a category used in accounting, trade, or law for goods and payments
senses.definitionCN: 会计、贸易或法律中用来分类货物与款项的类别
senses.example: Payment in kind means goods instead of money.
senses.exampleCN: 以物代款就是用货物代替钱支付。
senses.why: Commerce needs neutral categories, so the plain class word became a technical label for categories of goods.
senses.whyCN: 商业需要中性的类别词，于是这个普通的分类词成了货物类别的技术称法。

intro.en: Kind began as a word about birth and family, and only later came to mean a class of things.
intro.cn: kind 起初是关于出生和家族的词，后来才表示一类事物。

items.en: Old English gecynd meant nature, race, or inborn quality.
items.cn: 古英语 gecynd 指天性、族类或与生俱来的性质。

items.en: The same root produced kin, the word for family, which still shows the birth sense.
items.cn: 同一词根还造出了 kin（亲族），至今仍保留着出生血缘的意思。

items.en: The form shrank to kind, and the sense broadened from inborn nature to a class of things.
items.cn: 词形缩简为 kind，词义也从天性扩展到一类的物。

items.en: The classifying sense a kind of became the everyday one, while kindly kept the older sense of natural and gentle.
items.cn: 「一种」这样的分类义成为日常用法，而 kindly 保留了「天性温和」的旧义。

items.en: The spoken hedge kind of arose from the classifying phrase, used with no clear class in mind.
items.cn: 口语里表示「有点」的 kind of 由分类短语演变出来，用时心里并没有明确的类别。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the family of words sharing the root for birth and family; the near-meaning group holds other words for a class and for the kind heart.
note.cn: 形近组收共享「出生、家族」词根的词族；近义组收其他表示类别与善意的词。

entries.definition: One's family or relatives, the oldest sense of the root.
entries.definitionCN: 亲族、亲属，是这个词根最古老的含义。

entries.definition: Relation by blood, or a group of the same nature.
entries.definitionCN: 血亲关系，或指同类的一群。

entries.definition: In a gentle, well-meaning way.
entries.definitionCN: 由 kind 加 -ly 构成，指和善地。

entries.definition: The quality of being gentle and caring.
entries.definitionCN: 由 kind 加 -ness 构成，指善心这个性质。

entries.definition: A category of things with a shared feature.
entries.definitionCN: 指有共同特征的类别，是最常用的一般说法。

entries.definition: A British-flavoured word for a kind.
entries.definitionCN: 偏英式的说法，口语里常与 kind 互换。

entries.definition: A particular maker's kind of goods.
entries.definitionCN: 指某一商家出品的品类，即品牌。

normalIntro.en: These hooks trace the word from birth and family to class, then to gentleness.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把词从出生、家族引到类别，再引到和善。

normal.en: Kin is the same root and still means family.
normal.cn: kin 同根，至今仍指亲族。

normal.en: Kindred keeps the old sense of kin and sort by birth.
normal.cn: kindred 保留了「同血统同类」的旧义。

normal.en: Kind of is a spoken hedge, not a class.
normal.cn: kind of 是口语里的缓和语，并不点出类别。

normal.en: Payment in kind is payment in goods.
normal.cn: 以物代款就是用货物付款。

normal.en: Kind as a noun has -s; as an adjective it has -er and -est.
normal.cn: 作名词复数加 -s，作形容词有 -er 与 -est。

abstract.en: A kind is a basket drawn around things that look like they were born together.
abstract.cn: 一个种类就是画在「像同一出身」的东西外面的一个篮子。

abstract.en: Nature became manner: the inborn nature of a person turned into a gentle manner.
abstract.cn: 天性变成态度：人的天生性情转成了和气的举止。

abstract.en: Naming a kind is a quiet claim that the world can be sorted.
abstract.cn: 说出一类，就是在悄悄断定世界是可以被分拣的。

examples.en: That kind of machine needs special oil.
examples.cn: 那种机器需要专用油。

examples.en: All kinds of people come to this market.
examples.cn: 各种各样的人都来这个市场。

examples.en: It is kind of cold in this room.
examples.cn: 这屋里有点冷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「看它」——看它属于哪一种，就是在分类

root: 古英语 gecynd，指天性、族类，与 kin 同根；中古英语缩作 kind，义从「天生性质」转为「一类事物」，和善义则由「天性」一层派生。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: a class of things, a sort of person, the spoken hedge, a shared nature or family, and a trading or legal category.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：物的类别、某类人、口语缓和语、同族同性质，以及贸易与法律上的类别。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: things born of one stock gathered in one basket.
core.cn: 核心意象：同出一脉的东西被收进同一个篮子。

branches.en: THE BIRTH LINE: same origin makes things of one kind.
branches.cn: 出身这条线：同源让事物成为同类。

branches.en: THE PERSON LINE: sorting people by character.
branches.cn: 人这条线：按性格给人分类。

branches.en: THE HEDGE LINE: a vague class left open.
branches.cn: 含糊这条线：留下一个不明确的类别。

branches.en: THE LEDGER LINE: a neutral category for goods and payment.
branches.cn: 账簿这条线：货物与付款的中性类别。

branches.en: THE SHOP LINE: the same classifying act in a shop and in a ledger.
branches.cn: 店铺这条线：店里分货与账上分类是同一个动作。

intro.en: Kind is a short native root; English builds on it with -ly, -ness, un-, and old compounds such as kindred.
intro.cn: kind 是短小的本土词根，英语用 -ly、-ness、un- 以及 kindred 之类旧复合词在它上面造词。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic, so the Latin forms below are given only as contrasts to the real family.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词根属于日耳曼语，下面列出的拉丁形式仅作真实词族的对照。

items.example: It is a friend of a kind.

latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉丁语「出生、族类」，与 kind 意义相近而不同源
拉丁语「天性」，只是意义上与 kind 的旧义对照

definition_zh: 善意；仁慈；亲切的行为
definition_en: the quality of being warm and helpful, and an act that shows it
core_image: 雨里有人把伞悄悄偏过去半个伞面
scene: 车棚下只有一把伞，撑伞的人往旁边挪了挪。Her small kindness, sharing one umbrella in the rain, made the whole walk bearable.
sceneCN: 这里 kindness 是「善意的举动」（第 2 个义项：体现善意的行为），句意是她雨中同撑一把伞的小小善意让整段路都变得好过了。画面里有车棚、一把伞和被雨打湿的肩头。

derivatives.zh: kindness 由 kind 加 -ness 构成，词基指和善的
由 kind 加 -ly 构成，指和善地，与名词 kindness 分工
un- 加 kindness 构成，指不厚道、刻薄
由 kindly 加 -ness 构成，与 kindness 近义但更书面

senses.title: The quality of being warm-hearted
senses.definition: the quality of caring about others and wanting to help them
senses.definitionCN: 关心他人并愿意相助的品质
senses.example: Kindness runs in that family.
senses.exampleCN: 那家人代代都心善。
senses.why: The suffix -ness turns the adjective for a warm nature into the name of that nature itself.
senses.whyCN: -ness 把表示温和天性的形容词变成了这种天性本身的名字。

senses.title: A concrete act that shows it
senses.definition: a specific helpful act, counted one by one
senses.definitionCN: 一次一次可数的具体帮助行为
senses.example: She did him a kindness and asked for nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 她帮了他一个忙，什么也没要。
senses.why: English lets one suffix name both a quality and its instances, so the noun counts acts as well as moods.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许同一个后缀既指性质又指具体事例，所以这个名词既能量举动也能量心态。

senses.title: Gentle treatment of the vulnerable
senses.definition: the care given to animals, children, or the sick because they cannot repay it
senses.definitionCN: 因为对方无力回报而对动物、孩子或病人给予的照顾
senses.example: He treats old horses with great kindness.
senses.exampleCN: 他对老马十分体贴。
senses.why: Kindness is most visible where it cannot be repaid, so the word is drawn to the weak and the dependent.
senses.whyCN: 善意在无法回报的地方最显眼，所以这个词被引向弱小和依赖者。

senses.title: A softening habit in speech
senses.definition: the habit of saying things so that no one is humiliated
senses.definitionCN: 习惯把话说得不让任何人难堪
senses.example: There was kindness even in his refusal.
senses.exampleCN: 就连他拒绝时也带着体贴。
senses.why: Because kindness is judged by its effect on listeners, a way of phrasing counts as the quality itself.
senses.whyCN: 因为善意要看听者的感受，所以一种措辞方式本身也算作这种品质。

senses.title: Both the giving and the receiving
senses.definition: the relationship opened up when one person helps and another accepts help
senses.definitionCN: 一人给予、另一人接受时所形成的关系
senses.example: Kindness given freely usually comes back.
senses.exampleCN: 白给的善意往往会回来。
senses.why: The word names a bond rather than a single person, because the act needs two sides to exist.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是一种关系而非一个人，因为这种行为需要两边才能成立。
