intro.en: Kindness is a native English formation: the old word for inborn nature, given the suffix that names a quality.
intro.cn: kindness 是英语本土构成：把表示天生天性的旧词，配上表示性质的后缀。

items.en: The base gecynd meant nature or inborn quality, the same root that gives kin.
items.cn: 词基 gecynd 指天性、天生的品质，与 kin 同根。

items.en: The shortened form kind developed the sense of gentle and well-disposed.
items.cn: 缩简形式 kind 发展出「温和、心地好」的义项。

items.en: The suffix -nes, later -ness, named a quality, so kindnes meant a gentle disposition.
items.cn: 后缀 -nes 后作 -ness，表示性质，于是 kindnes 指温和的性情。

items.en: The countable sense of an act of kindness appears as the word spreads into everyday courtesy talk.
items.cn: 随这个词进入日常礼貌用语，出现了可数的「一件善举」义。

items.en: Kindness of strangers became a fixed phrase in English writing on city life.
items.cn: 「陌生人的善意」在书写城市生活的英语里成为固定说法。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the -ness and -ly family built on kind; the near-meaning group holds other words for goodwill.
note.cn: 形近组收由 kind 加 -ness、-ly 的词族；近义组收其他表示好意的词。

entries.definition: The adjective and noun behind this quality word.
entries.definitionCN: 这个品质词所依赖的形容词与名词。

entries.definition: The adverb, warm in manner.
entries.definitionCN: 同族的副词，指和善地。

entries.definition: A near twin, built from kindly plus -ness.
entries.definitionCN: 由 kindly 加 -ness 构成的近义双胞胎词。

entries.definition: Family, the oldest sense of the root.
entries.definitionCN: 亲族，是这个词根最古老的含义。

entries.definition: Moral good quality, wider and more general.
entries.definitionCN: 指道德上的善，范围更宽更泛。

entries.definition: A free and giving spirit, often with money.
entries.definitionCN: 指大方慷慨，常与钱财有关。

entries.definition: Deep sympathy for someone who suffers.
entries.definitionCN: 指对受苦者的深切同情。

entries.definition: The deliberate causing of pain, the reverse of kindness.
entries.definitionCN: 指故意施加痛苦，是 kindness 的反面。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the -ness suffix to a root about inborn nature, and to the small acts people notice.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把 -ness 后缀系在表示天性的词根上，也系在人们看得见的小举动上。

normal.en: Kind plus -ness names a quality, not a person.
normal.cn: kind 加 -ness 命名的是性质，不是人。

normal.en: Kindly and kindness split adverb from noun.
normal.cn: kindly 与 kindness 一个是副词一个是名词。

normal.en: Unkindness adds un- for the harsh opposite.
normal.cn: unkindness 加 un- 表示刻薄的反面。

normal.en: An act of kindness counts one helpful deed.
normal.cn: an act of kindness 数的是具体的一件好事。

normal.en: Out of kindness explains the motive, not the action.
normal.cn: out of kindness 说明的是动机而非行动。

abstract.en: Kindness is an umbrella tipped a little toward the other shoulder.
abstract.cn: 善意就是把伞稍稍偏向别人的肩。

abstract.en: A quality word with a countable sense means it can be counted in deeds.
abstract.cn: 一个能计数的性质词，意味着它可以按举动来数。

abstract.en: Kin and kindness come from one root: warmth begins with those nearest.
abstract.cn: kin 与 kindness 同源：温暖从最近的人开始。

examples.en: He never forgot her kindness in that hard year.
examples.cn: 那艰难的一年里她的善意他从未忘记。

examples.en: Small kindnesses make a long journey lighter.
examples.cn: 小小的善举让漫长的旅程轻快些。

examples.en: She thanked the nurse for her kindness.
examples.cn: 她感谢护士的照顾和善意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肯得奈斯」——肯得下心把好先给人，就是善意

root: 古英语 gecynd（天性）派生 kind，加名词后缀 -ness（古英语 -nes）构成 kindness，由「天生温和的性情」扩展出「善举」的可数用法；与 kin 同根。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: the quality itself, a countable helpful act, care for the weak, a softening way of speech, and the bond between giver and receiver.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：品质本身、可数的善举、对弱者的照顾、说话留余地的习惯，以及施与受之间的关系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: warmth offered from one person's hand to another's.
core.cn: 核心意象：暖意从一个人的手递到另一个人的手上。

branches.en: THE QUALITY LINE: a mood and its countable deeds.
branches.cn: 品质这条线：一种心态和可数的举动。

branches.en: THE WEAK LINE: care where nothing can be repaid.
branches.cn: 弱者这条线：得不到回报处的照顾。

branches.en: THE VOICE LINE: kindness heard in phrasing.
branches.cn: 声音这条线：从措辞里听到的体贴。

branches.en: THE BOND LINE: an act that needs two sides.
branches.cn: 关系这条线：必须有两边才成立的行为。

branches.en: THE LIFE LINE: from inborn nature to a returned favour.
branches.cn: 生活这条线：从天生性情到回报的好意。

intro.en: The word is one root plus one suffix, so the items show the root, the suffix, the negated form, and the near doublet.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个词根加一个后缀，下面列出词根、后缀、否定形式与近义的双胞胎词。

latinIntro.en: Both root and suffix are Germanic, so no true Latin family exists; the entries below are contrasts only.
latinIntro.cn: 词根与后缀都属日耳曼语，因此没有真正的拉丁词族，下面的条目只是对照。

items.exampleCN: 他的善举一件件累积起来。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉丁语「善意、宽厚」，与 kindness 只是意义相应
拉丁语「仁厚、教养」，仅作意义上的对照

definition_zh: 国王；君主；（纸牌中的）K；某领域最有影响者
definition_en: a man who rules a country by inherited right, and by extension the leading figure in some field
core_image: 王座上的人握着权杖，脚下铺着红毯
scene: 古堡大厅里，侍从把王冠捧到石阶之上。The old king sat on the throne while the hall fell silent.
sceneCN: 这里 king 是「国王」（第 1 个义项：世袭统治一个国家的男子），句意是老国王坐在王座上，大厅随之安静下来。画面里有古堡大厅、王冠、石阶和红毯。

pos.zh: 某领域中最有影响力的人或物

derivatives.zh: king 加 -dom 构成，指王国、领域
king 加 -ly 构成，指君王般的、威严的
king 加 -ship 构成，指王位、王者身份
king 与 fisher 合成的鸟名，传说为水上的「渔王」
king 与 pin 合成，原指车轴主销，今喻组织中关键人物

senses.title: A man who rules by inherited right
senses.definition: a man who rules a country because he inherited the position
senses.definitionCN: 因继承而统治一个国家的男子
senses.example: The king ruled for forty years.
senses.exampleCN: 那位国王在位四十年。
senses.why: The word began as the name of a tribal chieftain, and kingship stayed a matter of birth rather than election.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初指部落首领，而王位始终靠出身而非推举。

senses.title: The leading ruler of a nation
senses.definition: the head of state in a monarchy, whether ruling or symbolic
senses.definitionCN: 君主制国家的元首，或掌实权或仅作象征
senses.example: The king opens parliament each year.
senses.exampleCN: 国王每年为议会揭幕。
senses.why: As monarchies became constitutional, the same title kept its place while its power shrank to ceremony.
senses.whyCN: 君主立宪之后，同一称号保留下来，而权力缩小到仪式层面。

senses.title: The highest playing card
senses.definition: the card ranking just below the ace in a suit
senses.definitionCN: 同一花色中仅次于 A 的高牌
senses.example: He laid down the king of hearts.
senses.exampleCN: 他甩出了红桃 K。
senses.why: Card games copied social ranks, so the top of the court cards bears the ruler's name.
senses.whyCN: 纸牌游戏照搬社会等级，所以花牌最上面那张用了君主的名字。

senses.title: The most important chess piece
senses.definition: the piece that must be protected, though it moves only one square
senses.definitionCN: 必须被保护的那个棋子，虽然每步只走一格
senses.example: Losing the king ends the game.
senses.exampleCN: 丢了王，棋局就结束。
senses.why: The chess piece is named for the ruler because the whole contest revolves around protecting him.
senses.whyCN: 这个棋子以君主命名，因为整盘棋都围绕保护他展开。

senses.title: The dominant figure in a field
senses.definition: the person or firm thought to be the best or most powerful in an area
senses.definitionCN: 被认为是某方面最出色或最有势力的人或企业
senses.example: He was once the king of late-night radio.
senses.exampleCN: 他曾是深夜广播的王者。
senses.why: Because a king stands at the top of a hierarchy, the word transfers to any field with a top spot.
senses.whyCN: 因为国王处在等级顶端，这个词就挪用到任何有高下之分的地方。

senses.title: The largest size of something
senses.definition: an unusually large version of a product, as in king-size
senses.definitionCN: 比通常更大的商品规格，如特大号床
senses.example: They sleep in a king-size bed.
senses.exampleCN: 他们睡一张特大号床。
senses.why: Advertisers borrowed royal rank to mean bigger than the others, an old habit in trade names.
senses.whyCN: 商家借王者的等级来表示「比别的大」，这是商品名里由来已久的习惯。

senses.title: The figure who presides at a festivity
senses.definition: someone chosen to play the ruler in a game or celebration, such as a carnival king
senses.definitionCN: 在游戏或庆典中被选来扮演统治者的人，如狂欢节的王
senses.example: The carnival king waved from the float.
senses.exampleCN: 狂欢节的王在花车上挥手。
senses.why: Festivals have long borrowed royal titles for temporary honour, so the word became a role anyone can hold for a night.
senses.whyCN: 节庆早已借用帝王头衔来给人一时的荣誉，于是这个词成了一个谁都能当晚扮演的角色。

senses.title: The male of a bee or ant colony
senses.definition: an old term for the reproductive male of some social insects
senses.definitionCN: 旧时对某些社会性昆虫繁殖雄性的称呼
senses.example: Older books speak of a bee king.
senses.exampleCN: 较早的书里提到「蜂王」时指雄蜂。
senses.why: Early observers assumed every colony had a ruler, so they named a king before they recognised the female queen.
senses.whyCN: 早期观察者以为每个群体都有一个统治者，在认出女王之前先用「王」来称呼。

intro.en: King is one of the oldest Germanic words in English, a family and tribal title that predates the word country itself.
intro.cn: king 是英语里最古老的日耳曼词之一，是比「国家」这个词还早的家族与部落称号。

items.en: The Germanic form kuningaz meant a man of the kin, the head of a clan.
items.cn: 日耳曼语形式 kuningaz 意为「同族之人中的头领」，即氏族之长。

items.en: In Old English the word was cyning, and it named the ruler of a people rather than of a state.
items.cn: 古英语里这个词作 cyning，指的是一个民族的统治者而不是国家的元首。

items.en: Religious writing extended the title to God, giving phrases such as king of heaven.
items.cn: 宗教文本把这一称号扩用于上帝，产生「天国之君」一类说法。

items.en: The form settled as king, and the plural became kings.
items.cn: 词形固定为 king，复数作 kings。

items.en: With constitutional monarchy the title kept its rank while political power moved to parliament.
items.cn: 君主立宪之后，这一称号保住位次，政治权力则转往议会。

items.en: The word spread into cards, chess, and commerce as a label for whatever stands at the top.
items.cn: 这个词又扩到纸牌、象棋和商业里，泛指处在顶端者。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words formed from the same root and the same court; the near-meaning group holds other titles of authority.
note.cn: 形近组收由同一词根和同一宫廷体系构成的词；近义组收其他表示权力的称号。

entries.definition: The realm a king rules, built with -dom.
entries.definitionCN: 国王所统治的疆域，加 -dom 构成。

entries.definition: Family, the older sense inside the word for king.
entries.definitionCN: 亲族，是 king 一词内层更早的含义。

entries.definition: Fit for a king, royal in manner.
entries.definitionCN: 君王般的、威严的。

entries.definition: The female ruler, from an unrelated old root.
entries.definitionCN: 指女性君主，词根不同，与 king 成对使用。

entries.definition: A single ruler of a state, the general term.
entries.definitionCN: 指国家唯一的统治者，是最概括的说法。

entries.definition: A ruler above kings, historically of an empire.
entries.definitionCN: 指高于国王的统治者，历史上多与帝国相连。

entries.definition: The leader of a clan or tribe, close to the earliest sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指氏族或部落首领，接近 king 最早的义项。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build from the clan head, through the court, to cards and commerce.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从氏族之长出发，经过宫廷，走到牌桌与商场。

normal.en: King and kin share a root: a king is the head of the kin.
normal.cn: king 与 kin 同根：王就是族人中的头。

normal.en: The -dom in kingdom means domain and state.
normal.cn: kingdom 里的 -dom 表示领域与国度。

normal.en: Kingship is the office, king the person.
normal.cn: kingship 指王位这个职位，king 指人。

normal.en: The king in cards sits just under the ace.
normal.cn: 牌里的 K 正好排在 A 之下。

normal.en: King-size means the biggest size sold.
normal.cn: king-size 就是能买到的最大号。

abstract.en: A crown is a circle worn on the head, a shape the whole people could wear.
abstract.cn: 王冠是戴在一人头上的圆圈，而那个圈本来人人可戴。

abstract.en: A king in chess moves one square and rules the whole board.
abstract.cn: 象棋里的王一步只走一格，却统辖整个棋盘。

abstract.en: Titles drift from thrones to shop windows without changing their shape.
abstract.cn: 称号从王座漂到橱窗，形状却一点没变。

examples.en: The king gave the land to his younger son.
examples.cn: 国王把这片土地给了小儿子。

examples.en: She drew the king of spades on the last turn.
examples.cn: 最后一轮她摸到了黑桃 K。

examples.en: This city is the king of northern ports.
examples.cn: 这座城市是北方港口之王。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坑」—— 王坐的深坑只有一个人能坐，别人下去就出不来

root: 日耳曼语 kuningaz，意为「同族中的头领」，古英语作 cyning，由 cynn（族）派生；后由氏族之长扩指国家君主，并借到纸牌、棋类与商业中表「顶端」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses: the inherited ruler, the constitutional head, the top card, the chess piece, the leader of a field, the largest size, the festival role, and the old name for a bee colony male.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项：世袭统治者、立宪元首、最高牌、棋子、领域之王、最大号、节庆角色，以及旧书里对蜂群雄性的称呼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one figure above the assembled kin, holding the staff.
core.cn: 核心意象：族人围聚之中，一人立于其上，手握权杖。

branches.en: THE THRONE LINE: from clan chief to constitutional head.
branches.cn: 王座这条线：从部落首领到立宪元首。

branches.en: THE GAME LINE: the title copied onto cards and boards.
branches.cn: 游戏这条线：称号被搬上牌桌和棋盘。

branches.en: THE MARKET LINE: whatever is biggest borrows the royal rank.
branches.cn: 市场这条线：最大的东西借用王者等级。

branches.en: THE FESTIVAL LINE: a ruler for one night.
branches.cn: 节庆这条线：当一晚的统治者。

branches.en: THE HIVE LINE: a mistaken king before the queen was found.
branches.cn: 蜂巢这条线：在认出女王之前误认的王。

intro.en: King is a native root that builds freely with -dom, -ly, -ship, and compounds, which the items below lay out.
intro.cn: king 是本土词根，可自由加 -dom、-ly、-ship 并参与合成，下面逐条列出。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic with no Latin ancestry, so the Latin entries below are only Latin words for the same ruler.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词根属日耳曼语，没有拉丁血统，下面的拉丁条目只是同为「君主」的拉丁词。

items.example: The king called for his horse.
The kingdom stretched to the sea.
items.exampleCN: 这个王国一直延伸到海边。

items.example: A kingfisher flashed over the water.

items.meaning: a central pin or key person
items.example: He is the kingpin of the deal.
items.exampleCN: 他是这笔交易的关键人物。
它构成 kingdom 与 freedom。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉丁语「国王」，与 king 意义相当但不同源
拉丁语「王国、统治」，对应 kingdom 一义

definition_zh: 吻；接吻；轻触；轻碰
definition_en: to touch someone or something with the lips, or to touch something lightly, as a ball brushing the rim
core_image: 一个人俯身，用嘴唇轻轻贴上另一个人的脸颊
scene: 车站的月台上，母亲蹲下来与远行的女儿道别。She gave her daughter a quick kiss on the cheek before the train doors closed.
sceneCN: 这里 kiss 是「吻、亲吻」（第 1 个义项：用嘴唇接触表示亲爱或问候），句意是车门关上之前她在女儿脸颊上匆匆一吻。画面里有车站月台、母亲与女儿。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「接吻、亲吻」
由动词加 -er 构成，口语中指「亲吻的人」，也指嘴
加 -able 构成，义为「值得一吻的、可爱亲人的」
合成说法，义为「披露私情的」

senses.title: To touch with the lips
senses.definition: to touch a person or thing with the lips as a sign of love, greeting, or respect
senses.definitionCN: 用嘴唇触碰人或物以表示爱意、问候或敬意
senses.example: He kissed his mother on the forehead before leaving.
senses.exampleCN: 他离开前吻了母亲的额头。
senses.why: The core act is a small, soft touch of the lips, the most intimate gesture of the mouth.
senses.whyCN: 核心动作是嘴唇一次轻而柔的触碰，是嘴部最亲密的动作。

senses.title: The act or sound of kissing
senses.definition: an act of touching someone with the lips, or the sound of such a touch
senses.definitionCN: 用嘴唇触碰某人的行为，或这种触碰发出的声音
senses.example: She sent the children a kiss before bedtime.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们睡前她送了他们一个吻。
senses.why: The verb became a noun by naming the gesture itself, a pattern English uses again and again.
senses.whyCN: 动词直接名词化，用这个手势本身来命名，这是英语反复使用的模式。

senses.title: To touch lightly
senses.definition: to touch something very lightly, the way lips would, without pressing
senses.definitionCN: 像嘴唇那样极轻地接触某物，而不用力
senses.example: The ball kissed the top of the crossbar and went over.
senses.exampleCN: 球轻擦横梁上沿然后飞了出去。
senses.why: Because a kiss is barely a touch, the word extends to anything that grazes another surface.
senses.whyCN: 因为吻几乎算不上用力一碰，这个词便延伸到任何擦过另一表面的东西。

senses.title: To part from someone with a kiss
senses.definition: in the phrase kiss goodbye, to depart from someone with a kiss, or to give something up
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 kiss goodbye，指吻别，也指放弃某物
senses.example: You can kiss goodbye to your quiet weekend.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以跟你安静的周末告别了。
senses.why: The farewell kiss became a compact idiom, and the second meaning treats a lost thing as something kissed away.
senses.whyCN: 告别的吻凝固成习语，第二个意思则把失去的东西当作被吻走的东西。

intro.en: Kiss is an old Germanic word, recorded in English before the Norman conquest and related to the verbs still used in German and Dutch.
intro.cn: kiss 是古老的日耳曼语词，在诺曼征服前已有英语记录，与德语、荷兰语里仍在使用的动词同源。

items.en: The verb appears as cyssan, with the noun coss, in the earliest English texts.
items.cn: 这个动词在最早的英语文本里写作 cyssan，名词为 coss。

items.en: The same root is found in German küssen and Dutch kussen, which shows a common Germanic origin.
items.cn: 同一词根见于德语 küssen 与荷兰语 kussen，说明它源自共同的日耳曼语。

items.en: Northern and eastern dialects kept short forms of the word, which fed the Middle English spelling with k.
items.cn: 北部与东部方言保留了短暂的词形，为中古英语带 k 的拼法提供了来源。

items.en: The form settle between Old and Modern English as kissen and kisse.
items.cn: 在中古英语时期，词形定作 kissen 与 kisse，处在古英语与现代英语之间。

items.en: English keeps the word for the gesture and adds idioms such as kiss goodbye and kiss and make up.
items.cn: 英语保留了这个手势词，并增添了 kiss goodbye、kiss and make up 等习语。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that differ from kiss by one or two letters; the near-meaning group collects other words for affection shown with the body or the lips.
note.cn: 形近组收与 kiss 相差一两个字母的词；近义组收以身体或嘴唇表达亲昵的其他词。

entries.definition: Formed directly from kiss with the suffix -able, meaning worth kissing.
entries.definitionCN: 由 kiss 加 -able 直接构成，义为「值得一吻的」。

entries.definition: An old Scottish word for a chest, spelled like the past tense of kiss.
entries.definitionCN: 苏格兰语里指「箱子」的旧词，拼法与 kiss 的过去式相同。

entries.definition: A fruit jelly once served at Russian meals, unrelated in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 曾经出现在俄式餐桌上的果冻，词源与 kiss 无关。

entries.definition: To hold someone in the arms, a bigger and more whole-bodied gesture.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人抱在怀里，动作更大、更整体。

entries.definition: A quick, light kiss, named after the bird.
entries.definitionCN: 轻快的一下亲吻，由鸟啄食的动作得名。

entries.definition: To touch someone gently with the hand, without the lips.
entries.definitionCN: 用手轻柔地抚摸，不涉及嘴唇。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Germanic family and the set phrases in which the word actually appears.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用真实的日耳曼语词族，以及这个词实际出现的固定说法。

normal.en: Kiss doubles the s before -es and -ed: kisses, kissed.
normal.cn: kiss 在加 -es 和 -ed 前要双写 s：kisses、kissed。

normal.en: German küssen and Dutch kussen keep the same root alive.
normal.cn: 德语 küssen 与荷兰语 kussen 把同一词根延续下来。

normal.en: The noun takes a modifier: a quick kiss, a goodbye kiss, a kiss on the cheek.
normal.cn: 名词常带修饰语：a quick kiss、a goodbye kiss、a kiss on the cheek。

normal.en: Blow a kiss sends the gesture through the air instead of the lips.
normal.cn: blow a kiss 是把这一手势吹出去，而不是用嘴唇贴上。

normal.en: A ball that grazes the rim is said to kiss it.
normal.cn: 擦过篮圈的球被说成对它 kiss 了一下。

abstract.en: A kiss is the smallest possible contact: two surfaces almost touching, and nothing more.
abstract.cn: 吻是可能的最轻的接触：两个表面几乎贴上，仅此而已。

abstract.en: The same word covers love and geometry; the gentleness is what the two have in common.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指爱情也指几何：两者的共同点就是那份轻。

abstract.en: To kiss something goodbye is to accept that it will not come back, as a farewell kiss marks a parting.
abstract.cn: kiss something goodbye 就是承认它不会回来，正如告别的一吻标志分离。

examples.en: She kissed her son goodnight.
examples.cn: 她吻了儿子，道一声晚安。

examples.en: The first kiss came after the film ended.
examples.cn: 电影散场后他们有了第一次亲吻。

examples.en: The shuttlecock kissed the net and dropped over.
examples.cn: 羽毛球轻擦球网后落到了对面。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「可斯」——轻轻可斯的一下，就是亲吻

root: 古英语 cyssan（动词）与 coss（名词），源自共同日耳曼语词根，同源于德语 küssen、荷兰语 kussen；中古英语写作 kissen、kisse，现代英语固定为 kiss，并引申出轻触与吻别义。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: the lips touching as a sign of love, the gesture as a noun, any very light contact, and the farewell idiom.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：以唇触碰表示亲爱，作为名词的手势本身，任何极轻的接触，以及告别的固定说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: lips resting for a moment on a cheek, the lightest touch the body makes.
core.cn: 核心意象：嘴唇在脸颊上停留一瞬，是身体能做出的最轻的触碰。

branches.en: THE LIPS LINE: the mouth touches as a sign of love, greeting or respect.
branches.cn: 唇线：嘴部触碰，表示爱意、问候或敬意。

branches.en: THE GESTURE LINE: the touch becomes a countable thing people give and send.
branches.cn: 手势线：这份触碰变成可以送出、可以计数的一个东西。

branches.en: THE GRAZE LINE: anything that barely touches, from a ball to a breeze, borrows the word.
branches.cn: 擦碰线：从球到微风，任何几乎贴上的东西都借用这个词。

branches.en: THE PARTING LINE: the farewell kiss turns into an idiom for giving something up.
branches.cn: 离别线：告别的吻变成放弃某物的习语。

branches.en: THE FAMILY LINE: the Germanic cousins keep the same root in German and Dutch.
branches.cn: 词族线：德语与荷兰语的同源词保留着同一词根。

intro.en: Kiss is a native Germanic word that grows mainly by inflection and by a few suffixes and compounds.
intro.cn: kiss 是日耳曼本土词，主要靠词形变化以及少数后缀与合成来扩展。

latinIntro.en: Kiss has no Latin ancestor; the Latin words below are given only as contrasts for the same idea.
latinIntro.cn: kiss 没有拉丁语祖先，下面这些拉丁词只是同一概念的对照。

items.example: The couple were kissing in the rain.
A kiss-and-tell article ruined his career.
items.exampleCN: 一篇披露私情的文章毁了他的事业。

items.example: They kissed goodbye at the gate.

definition_zh: 厨房；烹饪部门；某种风味的菜系
definition_en: the room where food is prepared and cooked, and by extension the cooking staff or the cuisine of a place
core_image: 灶台上蒸汽升腾，案板、锅铲与菜刀各在其位
scene: 傍晚的出租屋里，油烟机低声作响，水汽模糊了窗。In the tiny kitchen a pot of soup was simmering while she chopped spring onions on the board.
sceneCN: 这里 kitchen 是「厨房」（第 1 个义项：做饭做菜的房间），句意是在这间小厨房里一锅汤正炖着，她在案板上切小葱。画面里有傍晚的出租屋、油烟机和水汽。

pos.zh: 名词：厨房；炊事人员；菜系

derivatives.zh: kitchen 加指小后缀构成，义为「小厨房」
kitchen 与 ware 合成，义为「厨房用具」
古词，义为「管厨房的人」

senses.title: The room where food is cooked
senses.definition: the room in a house or restaurant used for preparing and cooking food
senses.definitionCN: 住宅或餐馆里用于备餐与烹饪的房间
senses.example: The smell of garlic filled the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 蒜香充满了厨房。
senses.why: The word names the place itself, the room built around fire and water for cooking.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指地方本身：围绕火与水而建、专门用于做饭的那个房间。

senses.title: The cooking staff of a place
senses.definition: the people who work in a kitchen, especially the cooks of a restaurant or hotel
senses.definitionCN: 在厨房工作的人，尤指餐馆或酒店的厨师团队
senses.example: The kitchen was praised for serving hot food all night.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房因整夜供应热食而受到称赞。
senses.why: In a restaurant the room and the people inside it are spoken of as one unit, so a good team simply becomes a good kitchen.
senses.whyCN: 在餐馆里，房间和里面的人被当作一个整体来说，于是好团队干脆就被称作好厨房。

senses.title: A regional style of cooking
senses.definition: the food and cooking style of a country or region
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家或地区的菜肴与烹饪风格
senses.example: She loves the Sichuan kitchen for its heat.
senses.exampleCN: 她喜欢川菜那股辣劲。
senses.why: Chefs began to speak of a whole national cuisine as a kitchen, and the metaphor stayed in food writing.
senses.whyCN: 厨师们开始把一个国家的整套烹饪称为一个 kitchen，这个比喻留在了饮食写作里。

intro.en: Kitchen descends from Latin coquina through Old English, and every step of the chain is recorded.
intro.cn: kitchen 由拉丁语 coquina 经古英语一路传来，这条链条的每一环都有文献记录。

items.en: Coquina was the Latin word for a kitchen, and coquere meant to cook or prepare food with heat.
items.cn: coquina 是拉丁语「厨房」，动词 coquere 意为用火烹煮。

items.en: English borrowed the food word early as cycene, with the same cooking sense as the Latin.
items.cn: 英语很早就借入这个词，写作 cycene，烹饪义与拉丁语相同。

items.en: Norse speakers in the ninth and tenth centuries reshaped the word, and their form lies behind the modern spelling.
items.cn: 九、十世纪的北欧移民改造了这个词形，现代拼法源自他们的形式。

items.en: Kitchene appears as the home room and, in great houses, as the whole cooking department.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 kitchene，既指家中的房间，也指大宅里整个厨房班子。

items.en: The word widens into cookbooks and menus: kitchen now also names a cuisine, as in the Italian kitchen.
items.cn: 这个词延伸到菜谱与菜单里：如今 kitchen 也指一种菜系，如意大利菜系。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that begin or end like kitchen; the near-meaning group gathers other rooms and places for food.
note.cn: 形近组收开头或结尾像 kitchen 的词；近义组收其他与食物有关的房间与场所。

entries.definition: The word plus a small-size suffix, meaning a tiny kitchen.
entries.definitionCN: 本词加表示「小」的后缀，义为「小厨房」。

entries.definition: Shares the first letters, but names a young cat.
entries.definitionCN: 前半段相同，指的是小猫。

entries.definition: An old word for a person in charge of a kitchen.
entries.definitionCN: 旧词，指负责管厨房的人。

entries.definition: A small room for storing food and dishes, not for cooking.
entries.definitionCN: 储存食物与餐具的小房间，不做饭。

entries.definition: The kitchen of a ship or an aircraft.
entries.definitionCN: 船或飞机上的厨房。

entries.definition: A place where meals are served to a group, such as workers or students.
entries.definitionCN: 为工人、学生等群体供餐的食堂。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded Latin and Old English chain and the phrases the word appears in today.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用有据可查的拉丁语与古英语链条，以及这个词现在的常见搭配。

normal.en: Latin coquere meant to cook, and its noun coquina was the kitchen.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 coquere 意为「煮」，其名词 coquina 就是厨房。

normal.en: Old English wrote it cycene, then Norse speakers changed the sound.
normal.cn: 古英语写作 cycene，后来北欧移民改变了读音。

normal.en: A kitchenette is a kitchen cut down to a corner.
normal.cn: kitchenette 就是缩到一角的小厨房。

normal.en: Kitchenware is everything in the kitchen except the food.
normal.cn: kitchenware 是厨房里除了食物以外的一切。

normal.en: In restaurants the word means the staff, not just the room.
normal.cn: 在餐馆里这个词指那班人，而不只是房间。

abstract.en: A kitchen is a room built as a tool: cupboards, heat, water and a surface to work on.
abstract.cn: 厨房像一件被盖成房间的工具：柜子、火、水，以及一块干活的面。

abstract.en: Of all the rooms in a house, only this one is named after the verb for cooking.
abstract.cn: 一栋房子的所有房间里，只有它是以「烹饪」这个动词的祖先命名的。

abstract.en: Order in the kitchen is a small image of order in the household: food ready when people need it.
abstract.cn: 厨房里的秩序是家庭秩序的小小缩影：人在需要时，饭已备好。

examples.en: The children ate breakfast in the kitchen.
examples.cn: 孩子们在厨房吃了早饭。

examples.en: The hotel kitchen serves dinner until eleven.
examples.cn: 酒店厨房供餐到十一点。

examples.en: This book explores the Italian kitchen region by region.
examples.cn: 这本书按地区逐一考察意大利菜系。

dict_mnemonic.text: kitchen 里总有 chicken——厨房里总有鸡肉香

root: 古英语 cycene，源自拉丁语 coquina（厨房）、coquere（烹煮），并受古北欧语形式改造；中古英语 kitchene，现代英语 kitchen，后引申指厨房人员与菜系。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the room, the team who work there, and a whole cuisine seen as one kitchen.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：那个房间，在那里工作的一班人，以及被看作一个厨房的一整套菜系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: steam over a pot, knives and boards laid out, the room built for cooking.
core.cn: 核心意象：锅上蒸汽升腾，刀与案板各就各位，这是为做饭而建的房间。

branches.en: THE ROOM: the place with heat, water and work surfaces.
branches.cn: 房间线：有火、有水、有操作台的地方。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE: in trade the word stands for the cooks as a body.
branches.cn: 人员线：在行业内这个词代表作为整体的厨师。

branches.en: THE CUISINE: a whole food culture can be spoken of as one kitchen.
branches.cn: 菜系线：整套饮食文化可以说成一个厨房。

branches.en: THE LATIN LINE: cook and kitchen come from the same root, coquere.
branches.cn: 拉丁线：cook 与 kitchen 同出一根，即 coquere。

branches.en: THE SMALL FORM: a kitchenette is the same room in miniature.
branches.cn: 小型线：kitchenette 是同一个房间的缩小版。

intro.en: Kitchen is an inherited Latin-French-Norse word, and English extends it with diminutive and compound forms.
intro.cn: kitchen 是经拉丁语、古法语与北欧语传下的固有词，英语用指小与合成形式扩展它。

latinIntro.en: Latin coquere and coquina are recorded, as are the derived forms below.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 coquere 与 coquina 均有记录，下面这些派生形式也同样有据。

items.example: It is part of the Latin source.
items.exampleCN: 它是拉丁语源词的一部分。

latinEntries.meaning: to cook, to prepare food with heat

definition_zh: 膝；膝盖；膝部；裤子的膝部
definition_en: the joint between the thigh and the lower leg, the front part of that joint, or the part of a garment covering it
core_image: 一条腿在弯折处凸起的硬骨，屈伸之间承担全身重量
scene: 球场上有人被铲倒，抱着腿蜷在草皮上。He fell on his knee and stayed down for a moment before standing up again.
sceneCN: 这里 knee 是「膝盖、膝关节」（第 1 个义项：大腿与小腿之间的关节），句意是他跪倒在地，停了一会儿才重新站起来。画面里有球场草皮与受伤的球员。

pos.zh: 名词：膝；膝关节；膝部；裤膝

derivatives.zh: 与 knee 同源的动词，义为「跪下」
knee 与 deep 合成，义为「深及膝盖的」
knee 与 cap 合成，义为「膝盖骨」
合成词，义为「条件反射式的、不经思考的」

senses.title: The joint of the leg
senses.definition: the joint where the thigh and the lower leg meet, which allows the leg to bend
senses.definitionCN: 大腿与小腿相接、能让腿弯曲的关节
senses.example: The old injury still makes his knee ache in cold weather.
senses.exampleCN: 旧伤让他的膝盖一到冷天就疼。
senses.why: The joint is the body part the word first named, and all other senses grow from it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早命名的就是这处关节，其他义项都由它生长出来。

senses.title: The front of the knee
senses.definition: the front area of the leg around that joint, where a person kneels
senses.definitionCN: 关节周围的腿部前侧，人下跪时着地的部位
senses.example: She rested the baby on her knee.
senses.exampleCN: 她把婴儿放在膝上。
senses.why: Because the front of the joint is what people rest things on, the same word names the lap-like surface.
senses.whyCN: 由于关节前侧是人放东西的地方，同一个词也用来指这块近似膝盖上的台面。

senses.title: The part of a garment over the knee
senses.definition: the part of a trouser leg that covers the knee
senses.definitionCN: 裤腿上覆盖膝盖的那一段
senses.example: The boy always wore out the knees of his trousers.
senses.exampleCN: 那男孩总把裤子的膝部磨破。
senses.why: Clothing takes the names of the body parts it covers, so trousers have knees as people do.
senses.whyCN: 衣物会借用它所覆盖的身体部位之名，所以裤子也有膝盖。

intro.en: Knee is an old Germanic body word whose k has been silent for centuries; related words survive in German and Dutch.
intro.cn: knee 是古老的日耳曼语身体词，词首的 k 已沉默数百年；相关词在德语与荷兰语中留存。

items.en: The noun was cneo, and the related verb cneowian meant to kneel.
items.cn: 名词写作 cneo，相关的动词 cneowian 意为「跪下」。

items.en: German Knie and Dutch knie show the same word in the other Germanic languages.
items.cn: 德语 Knie 与荷兰语 knie 显示同一词在日耳曼语其他分支中的样貌。

items.en: The spelling became kne and knes, and the k stopped being pronounced before the vowel.
items.cn: 拼法变为 kne 与 knes，词首的 k 在元音前已不再发音。

items.en: The silent k and the long vowel make knee look unlike the way it sounds.
items.cn: 不发音的 k 与长元音让 knee 的写法与读音显得很不一样。

items.en: English builds compounds from it, among them kneecap and knee-deep.
items.cn: 英语用它构成合成词，如 kneecap 与 knee-deep。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with the same silent k or a similar ending; the near-meaning group gathers other joints and related body words.
note.cn: 形近组收同样带不发音 k 或结尾相近的词；近义组收其他关节与相关身体词。

entries.definition: The verb from the same Old English root, meaning to go down on the knees.
entries.definitionCN: 与 knee 同出古英语词根的动词，义为「跪」。

entries.definition: Starts with the same silent k, but means to work dough with the hands.
entries.definitionCN: 同样以不发音的 k 开头，意为用手揉面团。

entries.definition: Another silent-k word, naming a cutting tool.
entries.definitionCN: 又一个 k 不发音的词，指刀具。

entries.definition: The part of the leg above the knee.
entries.definitionCN: 膝以上的那段腿，即大腿。

entries.definition: The front of the lower leg below the knee.
entries.definitionCN: 膝以下小腿的前面。

entries.definition: The joint of the arm, the knee of the upper limb.
entries.definitionCN: 手臂的关节，上肢的「膝」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English form, the silent k, and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用真实的古英语词形、不发音的 k，以及这个词常见的搭配。

normal.en: Old English cneo already had the k, which later went silent.
normal.cn: 古英语 cneo 本就带 k，后来这个音沉默了。

normal.en: German Knie keeps the k spoken, while English dropped the sound.
normal.cn: 德语 Knie 仍把 k 读出来，英语则把它丢掉。

normal.en: On one knee is the pose of a proposal or of rest.
normal.cn: on one knee 是求婚或歇息时的姿势。

normal.en: Kneecap and knee-deep are built straight from the body part.
normal.cn: kneecap 与 knee-deep 直接由这个身体部位构成。

normal.en: Trousers wear out at the knees, exactly where the body bends.
normal.cn: 裤子总在膝部磨破，那里正是身体弯折之处。

abstract.en: A knee is a hinge: the whole body weight travels through a joint the size of a fist.
abstract.cn: 膝盖是一处铰链：全身重量都经过这样一个拳头大小的关节。

abstract.en: The word is the same for the joint, the lap and the cloth over it, because clothing follows the body.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指关节、膝上，也指膝上的布，因为衣物是跟着身体走的。

abstract.en: Bending the knee is the oldest gesture of respect, which is why the verb kneel carries such weight.
abstract.cn: 屈膝是最古老的敬意姿态，所以动词 kneel 才有那样的分量。

examples.en: He hurt his knee during the match.
examples.cn: 他在比赛中伤到了膝盖。

examples.en: The child sat on her father knee and listened.
examples.cn: 孩子坐在父亲膝上听着。

examples.en: These trousers have reinforced knees.
examples.cn: 这条裤子的膝部做了加固。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泥」——跪在泥里，最先沾泥的就是膝盖

root: 古英语 cneo（膝），源自共同日耳曼语，同源于德语 Knie、荷兰语 knie；中古英语作 kne，词首 k 在元音前逐渐不发音，现代英语扩展出 kneecap、knee-deep 等合成词。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the joint itself, the lap-like front of it, and the part of a garment that covers it.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：关节本身，关节前侧那块像膝上的台面，以及覆盖它的那段衣料。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hard knob at the bend of the leg, carrying the body as it folds.
core.cn: 核心意象：腿弯处一块坚硬的凸起，在身体折叠时承担重量。

branches.en: THE JOINT: the hinge where thigh and shin meet.
branches.cn: 关节线：大腿与小腿相接的铰链。

branches.en: THE LAP: the front of the joint is where children and books rest.
branches.cn: 膝上线：关节前侧是放孩子、放书的地方。

branches.en: THE CLOTH: garments take the name of the body part they cover.
branches.cn: 布料线：衣物借用它所覆盖的身体部位之名。

branches.en: THE SOUND LINE: the silent k marks the Germanic history of the word.
branches.cn: 读音线：不发音的 k 标出了这个词的日耳曼来历。

branches.en: THE POSTURE LINE: kneeling and sitting on the knee both begin at this joint.
branches.cn: 姿态线：下跪与坐在膝上，都从这处关节开始。

intro.en: Knee is an inherited Germanic noun; its family is built by inflection and by compounds such as kneecap.
intro.cn: knee 是继承而来的日耳曼名词，其词族靠词形变化以及 kneecap 一类合成构成。

latinIntro.en: Knee has no Latin source, so the Latin joint words below are offered as contrasts only.
latinIntro.cn: knee 没有拉丁语来源，下面这些拉丁语关节词仅作对照。

items.meaning: the bone in front of the joint
deep enough to reach the knees
to go down on the knees

items.exampleCN: 它把 knee 变成 knees。

definition_zh: 刀；小刀；餐刀；用刀刺伤
definition_en: a cutting instrument with a blade and usually a handle, or to injure someone with such a blade
core_image: 一片薄刃贴着砧板落下，把菜切成两半
scene: 灶前的灯下，菜板上堆着切好的葱段。She wiped the knife on a cloth and put it back in the wooden block.
sceneCN: 这里 knife 是「刀、菜刀」（第 1 个义项：带刃的切割工具），句意是她在布上擦了擦刀，把它放回木刀架。画面里有灶前的灯、菜板与切好的葱段。

derivatives.zh: knife 的不规则复数，义为「多把刀」
knife 与 edge 合成，义为「刀锋；十分危急的处境」
pen 与 knife 合成，义为「小折刀」
knife 与 man 合成，新闻用语指「持刀者」

senses.title: A cutting tool with a blade
senses.definition: a tool or weapon with a sharp blade fixed in a handle, used for cutting
senses.definitionCN: 刀片固定在柄上的切割工具或武器
senses.example: This knife is too blunt to cut tomatoes.
senses.exampleCN: 这把刀太钝，切不动西红柿。
senses.why: The core object is a blade with a grip, the simplest tool humanity has ever made.
senses.whyCN: 核心物件是一片带握柄的刃，是人类造过的最简单的工具。

senses.title: A table knife for eating
senses.definition: a knife used at the table for cutting or spreading food, paired with a fork
senses.definitionCN: 餐桌上用来切或抹食物的刀，常与叉子配对
senses.example: Set a knife and fork beside each plate.
senses.exampleCN: 在每个盘子旁放一副刀叉。
senses.why: The tool entered the dining room and took on a fixed shape, with a rounded tip and a dull edge.
senses.whyCN: 这件工具走进餐厅并固定了形状：圆头、不锋利的刃。

senses.title: To stab with a knife
senses.definition: to wound or kill someone by pushing a knife into the body
senses.definitionCN: 用刀刺入人体使人受伤或死亡
senses.example: The attacker knifed him in the arm.
senses.exampleCN: 袭击者用刀刺了他的手臂。
senses.why: The tool name turned into a verb by naming the act of using it, a pattern English uses often.
senses.whyCN: 工具之名转为动词，用以命名使用它的动作，这是英语常见的模式。

senses.title: The blade in a machine
senses.definition: a cutting blade that forms part of a machine or tool
senses.definitionCN: 构成机器或工具一部分的切削刀片
senses.example: The knife on the cutter needs changing.
senses.exampleCN: 切割机上的刀片需要更换。
senses.why: Industrial parts keep the old name because their job is still to cut.
senses.whyCN: 工业零件沿用旧名，因为它们的仍是切割的活。

intro.en: Knife reached English from Old Norse, and its plural knives is one of the classic examples of English consonant change.
intro.cn: knife 由古北欧语进入英语，其复数 knives 是英语辅音变化的经典例子。

items.en: The Norse noun knífr named a short blade, and it came into English with the Norse settlers.
items.cn: 北欧语名词 knífr 指短刃，随北欧移民进入英语。

items.en: The native English word for a cutting blade was seax, which was gradually replaced by the Norse word.
items.cn: 英语本土表示刀刃的词是 seax，后来渐渐被北欧词取代。

items.en: The word appears as knif, and the k at the start had already stopped sounding.
items.cn: 这个词写作 knif，词首的 k 此时已不发音。

items.en: The plural knives shows the old rule that a voiceless f becomes v between vowels.
items.cn: 复数 knives 体现了旧规则：清音 f 在两元音之间变为 v。

items.en: The noun also became a verb, and today a person can be knifed in the street.
items.cn: 名词也转为动词，如今可以说有人在街头被刀刺伤。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers silent-k words and forms of the same word; the near-meaning group gathers other cutting tools.
note.cn: 形近组收同样 k 不发音的词与本词的其他形式；近义组收其他切割工具。

entries.definition: The irregular plural, with f changed to v.
entries.definitionCN: 不规则复数，f 变为 v。

entries.definition: Another silent-k word, naming a mounted warrior.
entries.definitionCN: 另一个 k 不发音的词，指骑士。

entries.definition: Starts with the same silent k and means a rounded handle.
entries.definitionCN: 同样以不发音的 k 开头，指圆形的把手。

entries.definition: The cutting part of a knife, or a whole cutting tool in formal use.
entries.definitionCN: 刀的切割部分，正式用法中也指整件刀。

entries.definition: A long bladed weapon held with both hands, far larger than a knife.
entries.definitionCN: 以双手握持的长刃武器，比刀大得多。

entries.definition: A cutting tool with two blades that close on each other.
entries.definitionCN: 两片刃对合的切割工具，即剪刀。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Norse origin, the voiced plural, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用北欧来源、浊化的复数，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Norse knífr replaced the native seax, which survives in Saxon.
normal.cn: 北欧语 knífr 取代了本土的 seax，后者只留在 Saxon 一词里。

normal.en: Plural knives changes f to v, as in wife to wives.
normal.cn: 复数 knives 把 f 变成 v，如同 wife 变 wives。

normal.en: The k is silent, as in knee, knit and knock.
normal.cn: k 不发音，和 knee、knit、knock 一样。

normal.en: A knife and fork is the fixed pairing on a Western table.
normal.cn: a knife and fork 是西餐桌上固定的搭配。

normal.en: Under the knife means having surgery, with the surgeon blade as the image.
normal.cn: under the knife 意为接受手术，用的是外科刀的意象。

abstract.en: A knife has two faces: one side feeds people, the other hurts them, and the same word covers both.
abstract.cn: 刀有两副面孔：一面养活人，一面伤害人，同一个词兼指两者。

abstract.en: Its usefulness lies in a single narrow line where all the force is gathered.
abstract.cn: 它的用处就集中在一条极窄的线上，所有力量都聚在那里。

abstract.en: Every cutting tool is a controlled accident: sharpness kept in a handle until it is needed.
abstract.cn: 每件切割工具都是受控的意外：锋利被收在柄里，直到需要时才放出。

examples.en: He cut the bread with a long knife.
examples.cn: 他用一把长刀切面包。

examples.en: The chef keeps her knives razor sharp.
examples.cn: 这位厨师的刀磨得极快。

examples.en: A young man was knifed near the station last night.
examples.cn: 昨晚一名年轻人在车站附近被人用刀刺伤。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奈夫」——一刀下去，菜就断成两截

root: 古北欧语 knífr（短刃），随北欧移民进入英语，取代了本土词 seax；中古英语 knif，词首 k 不发音；复数 knives 保留了 f 在两元音间浊化为 v 的旧规则；名词后转为动词。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: the cutting tool, the table version, the act of stabbing with it, and the blade inside a machine.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：切割工具本身，餐桌上的那一把，用它刺人的动作，以及机器上的刀片。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin sharp edge pressed along a board until the material parts.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道薄而锋利的边压着砧板，直到材料分开。

branches.en: THE TOOL: a blade in a handle, the oldest cutting instrument.
branches.cn: 工具线：柄上加刃，是最古老的切割器具。

branches.en: THE TABLE: the dining knife has a rounded tip and a dull edge.
branches.cn: 餐桌线：餐刀头圆刃钝。

branches.en: THE WEAPON: the same object turned against a body becomes a verb.
branches.cn: 武器线：同一物件转而针对身体，就成了动词。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: industry keeps the word for any cutting blade.
branches.cn: 机器线：工业界沿用它指任何切削刀片。

branches.en: THE FORM LINE: the plural knives shows f turning into v.
branches.cn: 形式线：复数 knives 显示 f 变 v。

intro.en: Knife is a Norse loan whose family grows by irregular plural, compounds, and a verb use.
intro.cn: knife 是北欧语借词，其词族靠不规则复数、合成与动词用法扩展。

latinIntro.en: Knife comes from Norse rather than Latin; the Latin cutting words below are contrasts, not ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: knife 来自北欧语而非拉丁语，下面这些拉丁语切割词是对照，不是祖先。

items.structure: knife with f changed to v
items.example: The knives are in the drawer.
He was knifed in the alley.
items.exampleCN: 他在小巷里被人用刀刺伤。
这起刀伤案震动了小镇。

items.example: He opened the letter with a penknife.

items.meaning: the sharp edge, or a critical state
items.example: The race is on a knife-edge.

items.exampleCN: 它把 knife 变成 knifes。

definition_zh: 敲；敲门；碰撞；撞倒；敲门声
definition_en: to hit a door or surface with the hand or an object, often to be let in, or to strike something and make it fall or move
core_image: 指节落在木门上，发出短促的三下响声
scene: 旅馆的木门半旧，走廊里亮着一盏昏黄的灯。He knocked three times, then waited until a tired voice told him to come in.
sceneCN: 这里 knock 是「敲、敲门」（第 1 个义项：用手或物件敲打门面以示意），句意是他敲了三下，等人用疲倦的声音叫他进去。画面里有旅馆走廊、木门与昏黄的灯。

derivatives.zh: 加 -er 构成，义为「门环、叩门者」
knock 与 out 合成，义为「击倒获胜；出众的人或物」
合成词，义为「可拆装的；压倒性的」
合成词，义为「闹剧式的、粗笨却结实的」

senses.title: To hit a door to be admitted
senses.definition: to strike a door with the hand so that people inside will open it
senses.definitionCN: 用手击门以让里面的人开门
senses.example: Someone knocked at the door just after midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 午夜刚过就有人敲门。
senses.why: The core act is a short strike on a hard surface, loud enough to be heard inside.
senses.whyCN: 核心动作是在硬面上短促一击，声音刚好让屋内的人听见。

senses.title: To strike something and hit it
senses.definition: to strike a thing or a person, often by accident or with some force
senses.definitionCN: 撞上某物或某人，常属意外或带有力量
senses.example: The branch knocked against the window all night.
senses.exampleCN: 树枝整夜撞着窗户。
senses.why: From hitting on purpose the word widens to any collision, whether intended or not.
senses.whyCN: 从有意击打扩大为任何碰撞，不论是否有意。

senses.title: To make something fall
senses.definition: to cause something to fall or move by striking it
senses.definitionCN: 击打使某物倒下或移开
senses.example: He knocked the cup off the table.
senses.exampleCN: 他把杯子从桌上撞掉了。
senses.why: A blow that pushes an object off its place is the same action aimed at the thing rather than the door.
senses.whyCN: 把东西打离原位的这一击，用的是同一动作，只是目标换成了物件而非门。

senses.title: A blow or a setback
senses.definition: an act of striking, or a difficulty that sets a person back
senses.definitionCN: 击打的动作，或使人受挫的困难
senses.example: The team took a heavy knock when its captain left.
senses.exampleCN: 队长离开后球队受到沉重打击。
senses.why: The noun keeps the physical blow and turns it into an image of bad luck.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了实实在在的一击，又把它转成厄运的比喻。

senses.title: The sound of knocking
senses.definition: the short sharp sound made by striking a door or a hard surface
senses.definitionCN: 敲击门或硬面所发出的短促响声
senses.example: A sharp knock came from the engine.
senses.exampleCN: 发动机里传来一声尖锐的敲击声。
senses.why: The sound is the most detachable part of the blow, so the word names it on its own.
senses.whyCN: 声音是击打中最能单独剥离的部分，于是这个词也单独指这种声音。

intro.en: Knock first appears in English in the Middle Ages, probably from a Germanic root for striking, and its k has been silent for centuries.
intro.cn: knock 在中世纪才出现于英语，可能源自表示「击打」的日耳曼语词根，词首的 k 已静音数百年。

items.en: The verb is not recorded in Old English, though the related noun cnocc named a lump or knock.
items.cn: 古英语中未记录这个动词，但相关名词 cnocc 指肿块或一击。

items.en: Knock appears in the fourteenth century with the sense of striking hard.
items.cn: knock 于十四世纪出现，义为「重击」。

items.en: A relation with German knacken and Dutch knakken, both meaning to crack, is generally accepted.
items.cn: 普遍认为它与德语 knacken、荷兰语 knakken（意为「裂响」）有关。

items.en: The phrase knock at the door fixes the everyday sense of asking for admittance.
items.cn: knock at the door 这一说法固定了「示意求入」的日常义。

items.en: Particles multiply the senses: knock out, knock down, knock over, and knock off.
items.cn: 小品词使义项增多：knock out、knock down、knock over、knock off。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers silent-k words and relatives; the near-meaning group gathers other verbs of hitting.
note.cn: 形近组收 k 不发音的近形词与同族词；近义组收其他表示「击打」的动词。

entries.definition: Starts with the same silent k and names a tied loop of rope.
entries.definitionCN: 同样以不发音的 k 开头，指绳结。

entries.definition: One letter away, meaning a special skill.
entries.definitionCN: 只差一个字母，意为「窍门、技能」。

entries.definition: The word plus -er, naming a door ring or a person who knocks.
entries.definitionCN: 本词加 -er，指门环或叩门者。

entries.definition: To touch lightly and quickly, much softer than a knock.
entries.definitionCN: 轻而快地触及，比 knock 轻得多。

entries.definition: To hit noisily and heavily, with a louder result.
entries.definitionCN: 重而响地撞击，声音更大。

entries.definition: To hit something with a dull, accidental thud.
entries.definitionCN: 偶然撞上，声音沉闷。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real phrase family, the particle combinations, and the silent k that runs through the word.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用真实的搭配家族、小品词组合，以及贯穿全词的不发音 k。

normal.en: The k stays silent, as in knee, knife and knot.
normal.cn: k 不发音，和 knee、knife、knot 一样。

normal.en: Knock at the door is the phrase for asking to come in.
normal.cn: knock at the door 是请求进屋的说法。

normal.en: Particles change the result: out is a fight, down is a fall, over is a spill.
normal.cn: 小品词改变结果：out 是打斗，down 是倒下，over 是打翻。

normal.en: Two negatives make a compliment: she is a knock-out.
normal.cn: 两重否定反成赞语：她是惊艳众人的人。

normal.en: A knock on the engine is a warning sound, not a touch.
normal.cn: 发动机里的 knock 是警告声，不是触碰。

abstract.en: A knock is a question asked in sound, and the silence after it is the answer.
abstract.cn: 敲门是用声音提出的问题，之后的那片安静就是回答。

abstract.en: Any collision is a knock, because the same short shock passes through two objects.
abstract.cn: 任何碰撞都是一次 knock，因为同一股短促的冲击从两个物体之间传过。

abstract.en: From a fist on wood to a setback in life, the word keeps the image of something arriving suddenly.
abstract.cn: 从拳头落上木板到人生受挫，这个词始终保留着「突然到来」的意象。

examples.en: Please knock before you enter the office.
examples.cn: 进办公室之前请先敲门。

examples.en: The wind knocked the flowerpot off the sill.
examples.cn: 风把花盆从窗台上撞了下来。

examples.en: There was a loud knock at the back door.
examples.cn: 后门上响起一声很响的敲击。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「闹克」——指节一闹，门就咚咚克响

root: 中古英语 knocken（始见于十四世纪，义为「重击」），可能源自日耳曼语中表示裂响的词根，与德语 knacken、荷兰语 knakken 相关；词首 k 不发音，后靠小品词扩展出 knock out、knock down 等义。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: knocking on a door, any striking collision, causing something to fall, a hit as a setback, and the sound itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：敲门，任何撞击，把东西撞倒，作为挫折的一击，以及那种敲击声。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: knuckles striking a wooden door, three short sounds in the quiet.
core.cn: 核心意象：指节落在木门上，安静里响起三下短声。

branches.en: THE DOOR LINE: a knock is a request to be let in.
branches.cn: 门线：敲门是请求被放进来。

branches.en: THE IMPACT LINE: anything struck may move, fall or break.
branches.cn: 冲击线：被击中的东西会移动、倒下或破碎。

branches.en: THE FORTUNE LINE: a blow becomes a setback in life.
branches.cn: 命运线：一击变成人生里的挫折。

branches.en: THE SOUND LINE: the noise of the blow can stand alone.
branches.cn: 声音线：击打的声音可以单独成义。

branches.en: THE FORM LINE: the silent k ties it to knee and knot.
branches.cn: 形式线：不发音的 k 把它与 knee、knot 连在一起。

intro.en: Knock is a Germanic verb that English expands mainly through particles and compounds, not affixes.
intro.cn: knock 是日耳曼动词，英语主要通过小品词与合成来扩展它，而非词缀。

latinIntro.en: Knock has no Latin source; the Latin striking words below are contrasts.
latinIntro.cn: knock 没有拉丁语来源，下面这些拉丁语击打词只是对照。

items.example: He was knocked out in round two.
They knocked down the old wall.
The cat knocked over the vase.

items.meaning: one who or a thing that

definition_zh: 知道；了解；认识；懂得；精通
definition_en: to have information or understanding in the mind, to be familiar with a person or place, or to have learned a skill well
core_image: 一个人忽然点头，脑中的疑问合上了口
scene: 雨夜的车站，两个陌生人挤在同一个屋檐下。I know the timetable by heart, so I told her which platform to wait on.
sceneCN: 这里 know 是「知道、了解」（第 1 个义项：头脑中掌握信息或事实），句意是我把时刻表记得很熟，于是告诉她该在哪个月台等。画面里有雨夜车站与同挤屋檐下的两个人。

pos.zh: 动词：知道；了解；认识；懂得；精通

derivatives.zh: 由 know 加名词后缀构成，义为「知识；了解」
过去分词转形容词，义为「已知的；知名的」
un- 与 known 合成，义为「未知的；不出名的」
加 -ing 与 -ly 构成，义为「故意地、明知地」

senses.title: To have information in mind
senses.definition: to have a fact, a piece of information, or an answer in your mind
senses.definitionCN: 脑中掌握某个事实、信息或答案
senses.example: Do you know where the nearest chemist is?
senses.exampleCN: 你知道最近的药店在哪里吗？
senses.why: The core sense is having something present in the mind, as opposed to guessing or looking it up.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是心中已有某事，相对于猜测或临时去查。

senses.title: To be familiar with a person or place
senses.definition: to have met a person, or to be familiar with a place
senses.definitionCN: 见过某人，或对某地很熟悉
senses.example: I have known her since we were children.
senses.exampleCN: 我从孩提时代就认识她。
senses.why: Familiarity is information gained by repeated contact, so the same verb covers people and places.
senses.whyCN: 熟悉是靠反复接触得来的信息，所以同一个动词兼指人与地方。

senses.title: To understand or be able to do
senses.definition: to understand a subject or to be able to do something through learning
senses.definitionCN: 因学习而理解某门学问或会做某事
senses.example: She knows three languages and plays the violin.
senses.exampleCN: 她懂三种语言，还会拉小提琴。
senses.why: Knowledge learned becomes ability, so knowing shades into being skilled.
senses.whyCN: 学到的知识化为能力，于是「知道」渐渐过渡为「会」。

senses.title: To recognise or identify
senses.definition: to be able to recognise someone or something when you see or hear them
senses.definitionCN: 看见或听见时能认出来
senses.example: I knew his step on the stairs before he reached the door.
senses.exampleCN: 还没到门口，我就听出他在楼梯上的脚步声。
senses.why: Recognition is a kind of knowledge applied at the moment of contact.
senses.whyCN: 认出是知识在接触的一瞬间被调用。

senses.title: To experience or have seen
senses.definition: to have experienced something, especially in the phrase to have known better days
senses.definitionCN: 经历过某事，尤用于 have known better days 一类说法
senses.example: This old house has known happier times.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老房子也曾有过更热闹的日子。
senses.why: To have known something is to have lived through it, which lets the verb extend to experiences.
senses.whyCN: 曾知道某事物即曾亲历它，这使这个词可以扩展到经历。

intro.en: Know goes back to a Proto-Indo-European root for knowing, and it is one of the oldest words English has.
intro.cn: know 可上溯到印欧语中表示「知道」的词根，是英语最古老的词之一。

items.en: The verb cnawan meant to know or recognise, and the k was still pronounced.
items.cn: 动词 cnawan 意为知道、认出，那时 k 仍发音。

items.en: German kennen and Dutch kennen keep the same sense in the modern languages.
items.cn: 德语 kennen 与荷兰语 kennen 在现代语言里保持同样意思。

items.en: The Greek verb gignoskein is a distant cousin, and the English suffix -gnosis in diagnosis belongs here.
items.cn: 希腊语动词 gignoskein 是远亲，诊断一词里的 -gnosis 亦出此源。

items.en: The past forms knew and known settle, and the k at the start falls silent.
items.cn: 过去式 knew 与过去分词 known 定形，词首 k 不再发音。

items.en: The noun knowledge grows beside the verb, and phrases such as as far as I know fix its uses.
items.cn: 名词 knowledge 在动词旁成长，as far as I know 等说法固定了用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers close spellings and forms of the same family; the near-meaning group gathers other ways of holding information.
note.cn: 形近组收相近拼写与同族形式；近义组收其他掌握信息的说法。

entries.definition: The past tense form, with the silent k and the silent w.
entries.definitionCN: 过去式，k 与 w 都不发音。

entries.definition: The past participle, with the silent k kept in writing.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词，书写中保留了不发音的 k。

entries.definition: Sounds the same for many speakers, but it is the word of refusal.
entries.definitionCN: 许多人口中读音相同，但那是表示拒绝的词。

entries.definition: To grasp how something works or what it means, deeper than having the fact.
entries.definitionCN: 弄懂某事物如何运作或含义，比只知道事实更深。

entries.definition: To identify something already met, one narrow use of knowing.
entries.definitionCN: 辨认出曾见过之物，是「知道」的一种窄用法。

entries.definition: To gain knowledge that one did not have, the step before knowing.
entries.definitionCN: 获得原先没有的知识，是「知道」之前的一步。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real root history, the irregular past forms, and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用真实的词根历史、不规则过去式，以及这个词常见的搭配。

normal.en: Knew and known keep the silent k in writing but drop the sound.
normal.cn: knew 与 known 书写保留 k，读音却舍弃。

normal.en: The same root gives knowledge, and the Greek cousin gives diagnosis.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 knowledge，希腊语远亲给出 diagnosis。

normal.en: Know about is general information; know somebody is personal acquaintance.
normal.cn: know about 是一般信息，know somebody 是个人相识。

normal.en: Know how to names a skill rather than a fact.
normal.cn: know how to 说的是技能，不是事实。

normal.en: As far as I know is the standard hedge in English conversation.
normal.cn: as far as I know 是英语对话里标准的留有余地的说法。

abstract.en: To know is to have the world already mapped a little inside, before questions arrive.
abstract.cn: 知道就是在问题到来之前，世界已在心里稍稍画好了一张图。

abstract.en: The word covers fact, person, skill and memory because all four are held in the same place.
abstract.cn: 这个词兼指事实、人物、技能与记忆，因为四者都放在同一处。

abstract.en: Learning fills the map, but knowing is what lets a person act without checking.
abstract.cn: 学习在图上补线，而知道则让人不必查看就能行动。

examples.en: Nobody knew the answer to that question.
examples.cn: 没人知道那个问题的答案。

examples.en: She knows this neighbourhood better than I do.
examples.cn: 她比我更熟悉这一带。

examples.en: He knows how to keep a secret.
examples.cn: 他知道怎么守住秘密。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弄」——弄明白了，就是知道

root: 古英语 cnawan「知道、认出」，源自共同日耳曼语，上溯印欧语表「知」的词根，同源于德语 kennen、希腊语 gignoskein；中古英语词首 k 静音，过去式 knew、过去分词 known 沿用至今。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: holding a fact, being familiar with people or places, having a skill, recognising, and having lived through something.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：掌握事实，熟悉人或地方，具备技能，认得出，以及亲历某事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something inside the mind is already in place before it is needed.
core.cn: 核心意象：需要之前，心里的某样东西已经就位。

branches.en: THE FACT LINE: information is held ready in the mind.
branches.cn: 事实线：信息在心里备好。

branches.en: THE FAMILIAR LINE: contact over time makes a person or place known.
branches.cn: 熟悉线：长期接触让人或地方变得「知道」。

branches.en: THE SKILL LINE: knowledge practised becomes ability.
branches.cn: 技能线：练过的知识成为能力。

branches.en: THE SENSE LINE: recognition applies stored knowledge to the present.
branches.cn: 感知线：认出是把储存的知识用于当下。

branches.en: THE LIFE LINE: what a person has lived through is also known.
branches.cn: 人生线：人亲历过的东西同样是「已知」的。

intro.en: Know is an inherited verb whose family grows through the noun knowledge and through prefixes and suffixes.
intro.cn: know 是继承而来的动词，其词族靠名词 knowledge 以及前缀、后缀扩展。

latinIntro.en: Know has a Germanic root, though the Greek branch below shares the same Indo-European origin.
latinIntro.cn: know 有日耳曼词根，下面希腊语一支也出自同一印欧语源。

items.example: A knowing smile crossed her face.
items.exampleCN: 她脸上露出心领神会的笑。
它把 know 变成 knowledge。
